source: Written 2026-10-23/24 by Claude Sonnet from our own summaries of the NC 2017 standards, and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.NC17.3.OA.1: Factors up to 10 only. Skills: equal groups, writing multiplication sentences, repeated addition, arrays, meaning of a product, and the commutative, distributive and associative properties. Strategies are tested as choices of expression or story, since text cannot ask a student to explain. Factors up to 10. Division and missing-factor questions left out (other standards). Arrays and groups are written in words.
notes.NC17.3.OA.2: Whole-number quotients only (no remainders), dividends within the one-digit multiplication facts (at most 81).
notes.NC17.3.OA.3: All one-step problems with factors and divisors up to 10 (products to 90). Two-step problems (3.OA.8) are deliberately left out.
notes.NC17.3.OA.6: Whole-number quotients only, products within 100; stories and written-out sentences only.
notes.NC17.3.OA.8: Only addition, subtraction and multiplication (multiplication facts within 100, sums and differences within 1000), as the summary names; no division. Letters stand for the unknown in the equation questions. Skills: multiply then add (3), multiply then subtract (6), add and subtract (4), add then multiply (3), two products combined (4), write an equation (6), work backward (4). Two-step stories with addition, subtraction and multiplication only (no division); products within 100, sums and differences within 1000.
notes.NC17.3.OA.9: Hundreds board and multiplication table patterns are described in words, not shown; the explaining questions are choice questions about reasons. The hundreds board and the multiplication table are described in words (rows of 10; rows and columns 1 to 10), as no picture can be shown.
notes.NC17.3.NBT.2: Sums and minuends are within 1,000 (one answer is exactly 1,000-based, a missing part). Estimates always say how to round.
notes.NC17.3.NF.1: All models (area strips, number lines, ribbons) are described in words. Answers that are fractions are written a/b.
notes.NC17.3.NF.2: Kept within the wholes 0 to 1 and denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, 8; pictures are written out as equal parts, shaded parts and marks on a number line from 0 to 1.
notes.NC17.3.NF.3: Denominators 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 only, as the grade uses them; all models are written out in words (equal parts, shaded parts, a number line split into equal parts). Skills (rough counts): missing number in an equivalent fraction 5, fractions equal to 1 5, fractions equal to whole numbers 6, identify equivalent fractions 4, area or length models 5, number line 3, explain why fractions are equal 2.
notes.NC17.3.NF.4: Denominators kept to 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and fractions at most 1. Number lines and fraction bars are described in words, not shown. The wholes-must-be-equal idea is tested in 2 questions.
notes.NC17.3.MD.1: Clock hands are described in words. Each question that reads a hand tells the student that each number stands for 5 minutes.
notes.NC17.3.MD.2: Customary units used: inch, foot, yard (length); cup, pint, quart, gallon (capacity); ounce, pound (weight). Conversions between units are left out (they are Grade 4). Ruler questions are written as marks on a ruler (whole inches only; fractions of an inch belong to a later standard).
notes.NC17.3.MD.3: Graphs are written out: a picture graph by its key and number of pictures, a bar graph by its scale and where each bar ends, a table or tally as a list. Making a graph is not tested (it cannot be drawn in text).
notes.NC17.3.MD.5: The pictures are written out as rows and squares per row. Answers are counts (area in square units); the standard does not use a length x width formula, so no side lengths in centimeters or inches are used (that is 3.MD.6 and 3.MD.7). Skills: count the squares in rows and columns (6), tiling with no gaps/overlaps (5), compare areas (5), missing rows or squares per row (4), squares still needed (4), area in square units (3), same area, different rectangles (3).
notes.NC17.3.MD.7: Rectangles are described by their sides or rows of unit squares, never pictured. Unknown-side questions (2) are written as a missing factor, not as division. Sides and products stay within 100.
notes.NC17.3.MD.8: Whole-number sides only. Kept to the two named skills (perimeter from sides, unknown side from perimeter) and their rectangle, regular-polygon, composite and story forms; no area questions.
notes.NC17.3.G.1: Grade 3: shapes are described by their sides, side lengths and square corners (no pictures). "Draw examples" is tested as choosing which description could be a drawing. Names are limited to rectangle, rhombus, square and "another quadrilateral"; no trapezoid, parallelogram or kite, and no perimeter or area.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: There are 5 vases. Each vase has 4 flowers. How many flowers are there in all?
questions.solution: There are 5 groups of 4 flowers. $4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 20$, which is $5 \times 4 = 20$.

questions.skill: Write a multiplication sentence for equal groups
questions.stem: Which multiplication sentence shows 5 groups of 3?
questions.solution: 5 groups of 3 is $5 \times 3$. Three added to itself 5 times is 15, so $5 \times 3 = 15$.

solve.work: 5 groups of 3 is 5 x 3 = 15; the others are 3x3, 5x5 and an addition.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Dev adds $9 + 9 + 9$. He could multiply instead. What is the total?
questions.solution: The number 9 is added 3 times, so the total is $3 \times 9 = 27$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: Which multiplication sentence matches an array with 4 rows and 8 columns?
questions.solution: There are 4 rows with 8 in each row, so the total is $4 \times 8 = 32$.

questions.skill: Meaning of a product
questions.stem: What does $4 \times 5$ mean?
questions.solution: In $4 \times 5$ the first number tells how many groups and the second tells how many are in each group: 4 groups with 5 in each group.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: Each pack has 10 pencils. Lena buys 3 packs. How many pencils does she have?
questions.solution: 3 packs with 10 pencils in each pack is $3 \times 10 = 30$.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Which addition sentence shows 3 groups of 6?
questions.solution: 3 groups of 6 means adding 6 three times: $6 + 6 + 6 = 18$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A tray of muffins has 4 rows. Each row has 6 muffins. How many muffins are on the tray?
questions.solution: There are 4 rows of 6 muffins. $6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24$, so $4 \times 6 = 24$.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Ben knows that $2 \times 9 = 18$. What is $9 \times 2$?
questions.solution: Numbers can be multiplied in either order and the product stays the same, so $9 \times 2 = 2 \times 9 = 18$.

questions.skill: Meaning of a product
questions.stem: Which story matches $2 \times 7$?
choices: 2 bags with 7 marbles in each bag
2 bags with 2 marbles in each bag
questions.answer: 2 bags with 7 marbles in each bag
questions.solution: $2 \times 7$ means 2 groups with 7 in each group, which is 2 bags with 7 marbles in each bag.

solve.answer: 2 bags with 7 marbles in each bag
solve.work: 2 x 7 is 2 groups of 7: 2 bags with 7 marbles each.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Ivy's array has 3 rows of 8 tiles, which is 24 tiles in all. Jon's array has 8 rows of 3 tiles. How many tiles are in Jon's array?
questions.solution: Turning an array does not change how many tiles it has. $8 \times 3 = 3 \times 8 = 24$.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: There are 7 days in a week. How many days are in 2 weeks?
questions.solution: 2 groups of 7 days: $2 \times 7 = 14$.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: Each bike has 2 wheels. How many wheels do 9 bikes have?
questions.solution: 9 groups of 2: $9 \times 2 = 18$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: Which array has exactly 15 dots?
questions.solution: $3 \times 5 = 15$. The others have 12, 12 and 25 dots.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: An array of stickers has 3 rows. Each row has 7 stickers. Which multiplication sentence matches the array?
questions.solution: 3 rows of 7 is 3 groups of 7, so $3 \times 7 = 21$.

questions.skill: Equal groups or not
questions.stem: Which shows equal groups?
choices: 4 bags with 3, 3, 3 and 4 apples in them
4 bags with 2, 3, 4 and 5 apples in them
4 bags with 3 apples in each bag
questions.answer: 4 bags with 3 apples in each bag
questions.solution: Equal groups have the same number in every group.

solve.answer: 4 bags with 3 apples in each bag
solve.work: Equal groups: each bag has the same number, 4 bags of 3 each.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Sam says $6 \times 3$ means 6 groups of 3. He adds 3 six times. What total does he get?

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Pat counts by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. How many 2s did Pat count?
questions.solution: Pat said five numbers, so she counted five 2s. $5 \times 2 = 10$.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: Each of 4 shelves holds 5 books. How many books are on the 4 shelves?
questions.solution: There are 4 equal groups of 5. $4 \times 5 = 20$ books.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: A dog has 4 legs. How many legs do 3 dogs have?
questions.solution: 3 groups of 4 legs: $3 \times 4 = 12$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: An array has 5 rows and 2 columns. How many dots are in the array?
questions.solution: Each of the 5 rows has 2 dots. $5 \times 2 = 10$.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: There are 6 cups. Each cup has 1 straw in it. How many straws are there?
questions.solution: 6 groups of 1 is $6 \times 1 = 6$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A window has 2 rows of glass panes. Each row has 4 panes. How many panes are in the window?
questions.solution: 2 rows of 4 is $2 \times 4 = 8$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A sheet of stamps has 2 rows. Each row has 10 stamps. How many stamps are on the sheet?
questions.solution: 2 rows of 10 is $2 \times 10 = 20$ stamps.

questions.skill: Write a multiplication sentence for equal groups
questions.stem: Which multiplication sentence matches $2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2$?
questions.solution: Five 2s added together is 5 groups of 2: $5 \times 2 = 10$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A tray of seedlings has 3 rows. Each row has 9 plants. How many plants are on the tray?
questions.solution: 3 rows of 9 is $3 \times 9 = 27$.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Kira adds $5 + 5 + 5 + 5$. What is the total?
questions.solution: Adding 5 four times is the same as 4 groups of 5: $4 \times 5 = 20$.

questions.skill: Write a multiplication sentence for equal groups
questions.stem: There are 4 plates. Each plate has 2 cookies. Which multiplication sentence shows how many cookies there are in all?
questions.solution: 4 groups of 2 is $4 \times 2 = 8$.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: Each spider has 8 legs. How many legs do 2 spiders have?
questions.solution: There are 2 groups of 8 legs. $2 \times 8 = 16$.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Which addition sentence shows 4 groups of 3?
questions.solution: 4 groups of 3 means adding 3 four times.

questions.skill: Meaning of a product
questions.stem: Which story shows $3 \times 4$?
choices: 4 boxes with 4 crayons in each box
3 boxes with 4 crayons in each box
questions.answer: 3 boxes with 4 crayons in each box
questions.solution: $3 \times 4$ means 3 groups with 4 in each group.

solve.answer: 3 boxes with 4 crayons in each box
solve.work: 3 x 4 = 3 groups of 4: 3 boxes with 4 crayons each. No option shows 4 groups of 3, so only one fits.

questions.skill: Meaning of a product
questions.stem: A shelf has 4 boxes with 6 pens in each box. In $4 \times 6 = 24$, what does the 6 tell you?
choices: The number of boxes on the shelf
The total number of pens in all
The number of pens in each box
The number of pens that were added
questions.answer: The number of pens in each box
questions.solution: In 4 groups of 6, the 4 is the number of groups and the 6 is the number in each group.

solve.answer: The number of pens in each box
solve.work: 4 groups of 6: the 6 is pens in each box.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Which has the same product as $3 \times 7$?
questions.solution: Changing the order of the factors does not change the product.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: Nora has 6 boxes of crayons. Each box holds 9 crayons. How many crayons does she have?
questions.solution: 6 boxes with 9 crayons in each box is $6 \times 9 = 54$.

questions.skill: Write a multiplication sentence for equal groups
questions.stem: Zoe puts 5 stickers on each page. She fills 7 pages. Which sentence shows how to find the number of stickers?
questions.solution: There are 7 pages with 5 stickers on each page, which is 7 equal groups of 5. The total is found by multiplying: $7 \times 5 = 35$.

solve.work: 7 pages with 5 stickers each: 7 groups of 5, 7 x 5 = ?.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Tom wrote $4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4$. He writes the same total as a multiplication sentence, $? \times 4$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Count how many times 4 is added: 7 times. So the sentence is $7 \times 4 = 28$ and the ? is 7.

solve.work: Count the 4s: there are seven 4s, so 7 x 4 = 28; the ? is 7.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: Which array has exactly 24 dots?
questions.solution: $3 \times 8 = 24$. The others have $4 \times 5 = 20$, $6 \times 6 = 36$ and $2 \times 9 = 18$ dots.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A garden has 9 rows of plants. Each row has 7 plants. How many plants are in the garden?
questions.solution: The garden is an array of 9 rows with 7 in each row, so $9 \times 7 = 63$.

questions.skill: Meaning of a product
questions.stem: Which statement describes $6 \times 4$?
choices: The total when 6 is added to 4
The total in 6 groups with 4 in each group
The number left when 4 is taken from 6
The total in 4 groups with 4 in each group
questions.answer: The total in 6 groups with 4 in each group
questions.solution: $6 \times 4$ is 6 equal groups with 4 in each group, so it is the total in those groups. It is $4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 24$.

solve.answer: The total in 6 groups with 4 in each group

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Which expression has the same product as $4 \times 9$?
questions.solution: Factors can be multiplied in either order, so $9 \times 4 = 4 \times 9 = 36$. The others are 13, 81 and 16.

questions.skill: Distributive property: break apart a factor
questions.stem: Rita thinks of $7 \times 6$ as $7 \times 5$ plus $7 \times 1$. What is $7 \times 6$?
questions.solution: $7 \times 5 = 35$ and $7 \times 1 = 7$. Adding them gives $35 + 7 = 42$.

questions.skill: Distributive property: break apart a factor
questions.stem: To find $8 \times 7$, Jo breaks the 7 into 5 and 2. Which expression shows her plan?
questions.solution: Breaking 7 into 5 and 2 gives 5 groups of 8 plus 2 groups of 8: $8 \times 5 + 8 \times 2 = 40 + 16 = 56$.

questions.skill: Associative property: three factors
questions.stem: Max finds $2 \times 3 \times 5$. He first multiplies $3 \times 5$. What is the product of all three numbers?
questions.solution: $3 \times 5 = 15$, then $2 \times 15 = 30$.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: Each of 7 tables has 4 chairs. How many chairs are at the 7 tables?
questions.solution: 7 groups of 4: $7 \times 4 = 28$ chairs.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Which addition sentence shows 5 groups of 7?
questions.solution: Add 7 five times.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Which equation shows the commutative property of multiplication?
questions.solution: The commutative property says the order of the factors can change: $6 \times 4 = 4 \times 6$.

questions.skill: Doubling strategy
questions.stem: Ria knows $4 \times 6 = 24$. She doubles it to find $8 \times 6$. What is $8 \times 6$?
questions.solution: 8 sixes is two groups of 4 sixes: $24 + 24 = 48$.

questions.skill: Associative property: three factors
questions.stem: Which pair of expressions are equal because of the associative property of multiplication?
questions.solution: The associative property says the factors can be grouped differently without changing the product.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: A baker puts 9 cookies on each tray. She fills 5 trays. How many cookies does she bake?
questions.solution: 5 groups of 9: $5 \times 9 = 45$.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Which addition sentence does NOT have a total of 24?
questions.solution: $4 \times 5 = 20$, not 24. The others are 24: $6 \times 4$, $8 \times 3$ and $3 \times 8$.

questions.skill: Distributive property: break apart a factor
questions.stem: Use $4 \times 5 = 20$ and $4 \times 4 = 16$ to find $4 \times 9$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A parking lot has 8 rows of parking spaces. Each row has 5 spaces. How many parking spaces are in the lot?
questions.solution: 8 rows of 5 is $8 \times 5 = 40$.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: A school has 10 classrooms. Each classroom has 7 computers. How many computers does the school have?
questions.solution: 10 groups of 7: $10 \times 7 = 70$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A sticker chart has 10 rows. Each row has 10 stickers. How many stickers are on the chart?
questions.solution: 10 rows of 10 is $10 \times 10 = 100$.

questions.skill: Distributive property: break apart a factor
questions.stem: Dev finds $3 \times 9$ as $3 \times 4$ plus $3 \times 5$. What is $3 \times 9$?

questions.skill: Distributive property: break apart a factor
questions.stem: Pete finds $5 \times 8$ as $5 \times 4 + 5 \times 4$. What is $5 \times 8$?

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: A frog jumps 3 feet each time. It jumps 8 times. How many feet does the frog jump in all?
questions.solution: Add 3 eight times, or multiply: $8 \times 3 = 24$ feet.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Dara counts by 3s: 3, 6, 9, and so on. What is the 8th number she says?
questions.solution: The 8th number is 8 groups of 3: $8 \times 3 = 24$.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: A tile array has 4 rows with 8 tiles in each row. Counting by 8s, which addition sentence finds the number of tiles?
questions.solution: There are 4 rows, so add 8 four times: 8 + 8 + 8 + 8 = 32.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: An array has 7 columns. Each column has 3 dots. How many dots are in the array?
questions.solution: 7 columns of 3 dots is $7 \times 3 = 21$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: Which array has the same number of dots as 5 rows of 4 dots?
questions.solution: 5 rows of 4 is 20 dots. 2 rows of 10 is also 20. The others have 18, 16 and 25.

questions.skill: Write a multiplication sentence for equal groups
questions.stem: A farmer plants 8 seeds in each row. He plants 6 rows. Which multiplication sentence shows how many seeds he plants?
questions.solution: 6 rows with 8 seeds in each row is 6 groups of 8: $6 \times 8 = 48$.

questions.skill: Meaning of a product
questions.stem: Which problem needs multiplication to solve?
choices: Jo has 5 crayons and gets 4 more. How many crayons does she have?
A box has 5 rows of 4 crayons. How many crayons are in the box?
Jo has 9 crayons and loses 4. How many crayons does she have left?
Jo has 9 crayons, and 5 are red. How many are not red?
questions.answer: A box has 5 rows of 4 crayons. How many crayons are in the box?
questions.solution: Rows of 4 crayons, 5 times, are equal groups, so multiply: $5 \times 4 = 20$.

solve.answer: A box has 5 rows of 4 crayons. How many crayons are in the box?
solve.work: 5 rows of 4 is equal groups: 5 x 4. Others add or subtract.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Which number makes this equation true? $8 \times 6 = ? \times 8$
questions.solution: The factors can be switched: $8 \times 6 = 6 \times 8$.

questions.skill: Associative property: three factors
questions.stem: Dev finds $2 \times 4 \times 3$. He multiplies $2 \times 4$ first. Which expression shows his next step?
questions.solution: $2 \times 4 = 8$, so the next step is $8 \times 3$.

questions.skill: Meaning of a product
questions.stem: Which problem can be solved with $4 \times 7$?
choices: There are 4 bags with 7 apples in each bag. How many apples are there in all?
There are 4 bags with 7 apples in all. How many apples are in each bag?
Sam has 4 apples and gets 7 more. How many apples does he have?
Sam has 7 apples and eats 4 of them. How many apples are left?
questions.answer: There are 4 bags with 7 apples in each bag. How many apples are there in all?
questions.solution: $4 \times 7$ means 4 groups of 7, so the total of 4 bags with 7 apples in each bag.

solve.answer: There are 4 bags with 7 apples in each bag. How many apples are there in all?
solve.work: 4 x 7 = 4 groups of 7: 4 bags with 7 apples each.

questions.skill: Equal groups: find the total
questions.stem: A store sells pencils in packs of 8. Ana buys 6 packs and her brother buys 3 packs. How many pencils do they buy in all?
questions.solution: Ana buys $6 \times 8 = 48$ pencils and her brother buys $3 \times 8 = 24$ pencils. Together that is $48 + 24 = 72$, which is also $9 \times 8$.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Kofi skip counts by 6s: 6, 12, 18, 24, and so on. What is the 9th number he says?
questions.solution: The 9th number counted is 9 groups of 6, so it is $9 \times 6 = 54$.

questions.skill: Repeated addition and multiplication
questions.stem: Zane adds $7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7$. Which multiplication sentence gives the same total?
questions.solution: The number 7 is added 9 times (there are 9 sevens, with 8 plus signs between them), so the total is $9 \times 7 = 63$.

solve.work: Count the 7s: nine of them, so 9 x 7 = 63.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A rectangle array of chairs has 7 rows with 8 chairs in each row. Then 1 more row of 8 chairs is added. Which expression gives the new total number of chairs?
questions.solution: The 7 rows have $7 \times 8$ chairs. The new row adds 8 more chairs, so the total is $7 \times 8 + 8 = 64$.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A rectangle array has 6 rows of 9 squares. One whole row is covered up. How many squares can still be seen?
questions.solution: With one row covered, 5 rows of 9 squares can be seen: $5 \times 9 = 45$.

solve.work: 6 rows of 9 = 54; covering one row of 9 leaves 5 x 9 = 45.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Jin has 6 groups of 4 stickers. Tess has 4 groups of 6 stickers. Which statement is true?
choices: Jin has more because he has more groups.
Tess has more because her groups are bigger.
They have the same number of stickers.
Tess has 2 fewer stickers than Jin.
questions.answer: They have the same number of stickers.
questions.solution: Jin has $6 \times 4 = 24$ stickers and Tess has $4 \times 6 = 24$ stickers. Changing the order of the factors does not change the product.

solve.answer: They have the same number of stickers.

questions.skill: Meaning of a product
questions.stem: There are 6 pots with 4 flowers in each pot. In $6 \times 4 = 24$, what does the 24 tell you?
choices: The number of flowers in each pot
The number of flowers added to each pot
questions.solution: The 6 is the number of pots and the 4 is the flowers in each pot. The product, 24, is the total number of flowers.

solve.work: 6 is the pots, 4 the flowers per pot, 24 the total number of flowers.

questions.skill: Distributive property: break apart a factor
questions.stem: Use $6 \times 4 = 24$ and $6 \times 3 = 18$ to find $6 \times 7$.

questions.skill: Distributive property: break apart a factor
questions.stem: Which expression equals $9 \times 8$?
questions.solution: Breaking 8 into $4 + 4$ gives $9 \times 8 = 9 \times 4 + 9 \times 4 = 36 + 36 = 72$.

questions.skill: Associative property: three factors
questions.stem: A box holds 3 rows of 2 cupcakes. A truck carries 7 of these boxes. How many cupcakes are on the truck?
questions.solution: Each box holds $3 \times 2 = 6$ cupcakes. Then 7 boxes hold $7 \times 6 = 42$ cupcakes.

solve.work: Each box has 3 x 2 = 6 cupcakes; 7 boxes x 6 = 42.

questions.skill: Distributive property: break apart a factor
questions.stem: Kim wrote $7 \times 8 = 7 \times 4 + 7 \times ?$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Break 8 into 4 and 4: $7 \times 8 = 7 \times 4 + 7 \times 4$. The ? is 4.

questions.skill: Meaning of a product
questions.stem: Which gives the greatest total?
choices: 7 bags with 6 apples in each bag
5 bags with 9 apples in each bag
8 bags with 5 apples in each bag
6 bags with 7 apples in each bag
questions.answer: 5 bags with 9 apples in each bag
questions.solution: $5 \times 9 = 45$. The others are 42, 40 and 42.

solve.answer: 5 bags with 9 apples in each bag

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: A seating array has 6 rows of 5 seats. Which statement is true?
choices: Turning the array gives 5 rows of 6 seats, and the total stays the same
Turning the array gives 5 rows of 6 seats, and there are 6 more seats
Turning the array gives 6 rows of 5 seats, and there are 5 fewer seats
Turning the array gives 11 rows of 1 seat, and the total stays the same
questions.answer: Turning the array gives 5 rows of 6 seats, and the total stays the same
questions.solution: $6 \times 5 = 5 \times 6 = 30$. Turning an array swaps rows and columns, but does not change the total.

solve.answer: Turning the array gives 5 rows of 6 seats, and the total stays the same
solve.work: 6 rows of 5 = 30. Turning gives 5 rows of 6 = 30, same total (commutative property).

questions.stem: A baker puts 6 buns in each box. She fills 5 boxes, then puts 3 extra buns in a bag. Which expression shows the total number of buns?
questions.solution: 5 boxes of 6 buns is $5 \times 6$. Then add the 3 extra buns.

questions.stem: An array of squares has 7 rows of 6 squares. Sara adds 2 more rows of 6 squares. Then she covers 5 squares. How many squares can still be seen?
questions.solution: 9 rows of 6 is $9 \times 6 = 54$. Covering 5 leaves 54 - 5 = 49.

questions.skill: Arrays: rows and columns
questions.stem: An array of squares has 9 rows and 8 columns. 2 whole columns are covered up. How many squares can still be seen?
questions.solution: 6 columns are showing, each with 9 squares: $9 \times 6 = 54$.

questions.solution: Each row has 6 plants, so 2 rows have $2 \times 6$ plants. Take that from all the plants, $8 \times 6$.

questions.stem: Which story matches $5 \times 3 - 2 = n$?
choices: Eva has 5 bags with 3 beads in each bag. She loses 2 beads.
Eva has 5 bags with 3 beads in each bag. She gets 2 more beads.
Eva has 5 beads and 3 beads. She loses 2 beads.
Eva has 5 bags with 2 beads in each bag. She loses 3 beads.
questions.answer: Eva has 5 bags with 3 beads in each bag. She loses 2 beads.
questions.solution: $5 \times 3$ is 5 bags of 3 beads. The $- 2$ means 2 beads are lost.

solve.answer: Eva has 5 bags with 3 beads in each bag. She loses 2 beads.
solve.work: 5 x 3 = 5 bags of 3 beads, then - 2 = loses 2 beads. Option 2.

questions.skill: Add, then multiply
questions.stem: Each child in a class gets 3 pencils. There are 6 girls and 5 boys. How many pencils are needed?
questions.solution: There are $6 + 5 = 11$ children. Then $11 \times 3 = 33$ pencils.

questions.skill: Multiply, then add
questions.stem: Each bag has 5 apples. Ben has 3 bags and 2 loose apples. How many apples does he have?
questions.solution: 3 bags of 5 apples is $3 \times 5 = 15$. Then $15 + 2 = 17$ apples.

questions.skill: Multiply, then subtract
questions.stem: Ana saves 2 dollars each day for 6 days. She spends 5 dollars on a game. How many dollars does she have left?
questions.solution: She saves $2 \times 6 = 12$ dollars. Then $12 - 5 = 7$ dollars are left.

questions.skill: Compare, then combine
questions.stem: Rob has 15 cards. Sue has 6 fewer cards than Rob. How many cards do they have together?
questions.solution: Sue has $15 - 6 = 9$ cards. Together they have $15 + 9 = 24$ cards.

questions.skill: Two products, then combine
questions.stem: Leo buys 2 packs of pencils with 4 pencils in each pack and 3 packs of erasers with 2 erasers in each pack. How many items does he buy in all?
questions.solution: Pencils: $2 \times 4 = 8$. Erasers: $3 \times 2 = 6$. Together $8 + 6 = 14$ items.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Sue bought 3 boxes with 5 pens in each box. After she gave some pens to her friends, she had 9 pens left. How many pens did she give away?
questions.solution: She bought $3 \times 5 = 15$ pens. She gave away $15 - 9 = 6$ pens.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: Jo had 20 marbles. He lost 6 marbles and then won 4 marbles. He now has $m$ marbles. Which equation matches the story?
questions.solution: Losing marbles takes away and winning adds: $20 - 6 + 4 = m$.

questions.skill: Multiply, then add
questions.stem: A room has 4 tables with 4 chairs at each table. 2 more chairs are by the door. How many chairs are in the room?
questions.solution: $4 \times 4 = 16$ chairs at the tables. Then $16 + 2 = 18$ chairs.

questions.skill: Compare, then combine
questions.stem: Sam has 9 stickers. Jill has 4 more stickers than Sam. How many stickers do they have together?
questions.solution: Jill has $9 + 4 = 13$ stickers. Together they have $9 + 13 = 22$ stickers.

questions.skill: Add, then multiply
questions.stem: Eli has 2 red balloons and 3 blue balloons. Each balloon costs 4 dollars. How many dollars do the balloons cost in all?
questions.solution: He has $2 + 3 = 5$ balloons. Then $5 \times 4 = 20$ dollars.

questions.skill: Multiply, then add
questions.stem: Mr. Ortiz plants 4 rows of tulips with 4 tulips in each row. He plants 3 more tulips by the gate. How many tulips does he plant in all?
questions.solution: 4 rows of 4 tulips is $4 \times 4 = 16$ tulips. Then $16 + 3 = 19$ tulips.

questions.skill: Multiply, then compare
questions.stem: Nell has 4 pages of stickers with 5 stickers on each page. Her brother has 3 more stickers than Nell. How many stickers does her brother have?
questions.solution: Nell has $4 \times 5 = 20$ stickers. Her brother has $20 + 3 = 23$ stickers.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: A farmer has 4 pens with 3 hens in each pen and $n$ hens in the barn. There are 20 hens in all. What is $n$?
questions.solution: The pens hold $4 \times 3 = 12$ hens. So $n = 20 - 12 = 8$.

questions.skill: Add and subtract in two steps
questions.stem: Nora has 12 beads. She finds 7 more beads and then gives 5 beads to her sister. How many beads does Nora have now?

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Tia read 4 pages each day for 3 days. Then she read some more pages. She read 17 pages in all. How many more pages did she read?
questions.solution: In 3 days she read $4 \times 3 = 12$ pages. The rest is $17 - 12 = 5$ pages.

questions.skill: Multiply, then add
questions.stem: Each basket holds 6 apples. A farmer fills 7 baskets and then picks 9 more apples. How many apples did he pick in all?
questions.solution: The baskets hold 7 x 6 = 42 apples. Then 42 + 9 = 51.

questions.skill: Multiply, then subtract
questions.stem: Maya has 40 dollars. She buys 3 books that cost 8 dollars each. How many dollars does she have left?
questions.solution: The books cost 3 x 8 = 24 dollars. Then 40 - 24 = 16.

questions.skill: Add, then multiply
questions.stem: Tickets for the fair cost 3 dollars each. Rosa buys 5 tickets on Friday and 7 tickets on Saturday. How many dollars does she spend on tickets?
questions.solution: Rosa buys 5 + 7 = 12 tickets. Each costs 3 dollars, so 12 x 3 = 36 dollars.

questions.skill: Two products, then combine
questions.stem: A store has 4 boxes of markers with 6 markers in each box and 3 boxes of crayons with 5 crayons in each box. How many markers and crayons are there in all?
questions.solution: The markers: 4 x 6 = 24. The crayons: 3 x 5 = 15. In all: 24 + 15 = 39.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: A theater has 6 rows with 9 seats in each row. 7 of the seats are broken. The theater has t working seats. Which equation matches the story?
questions.solution: All the seats are 6 x 9. The 7 broken seats are taken away. So 6 x 9 - 7 = t.

solve.work: 6 x 9 seats minus 7 broken: 6 x 9 - 7 = t (=47).

questions.skill: Add and subtract in two steps
questions.stem: A library has 120 books. On Monday, 35 books are lent out. On Tuesday, 28 books are returned. How many books are in the library now?
questions.solution: After Monday: 120 - 35 = 85. After Tuesday: 85 + 28 = 113.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Ravi had some stickers. He gave 8 stickers to a friend and then bought 15 more. Now he has 40 stickers. How many stickers did Ravi have at first?
questions.solution: Work backward. Before buying 15 more, he had 40 - 15 = 25. Before giving away 8, he had 25 + 8 = 33.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: Dev has some marbles. He buys 3 bags with 4 marbles in each bag. Now he has 25 marbles. Which equation can find m, the number of marbles Dev had at first?
questions.solution: Dev had m marbles and added 3 x 4 marbles. He now has 25. So m + 3 x 4 = 25.

solve.work: m plus 3 bags of 4 gives 25: m + 3 x 4 = 25 (m = 13).

questions.skill: Multiply, then subtract
questions.stem: A garden has 5 rows with 9 tomato plants in each row. Deer eat 14 of the plants. How many plants are left?
questions.solution: The garden has 5 x 9 = 45 plants. After the deer: 45 - 14 = 31.

questions.skill: Multiply, then subtract
questions.stem: Kai has 26 crayons. He puts 4 crayons in each of 3 boxes. The rest go in a drawer. How many crayons are in the drawer?
questions.solution: The boxes hold 3 x 4 = 12 crayons. The drawer has 26 - 12 = 14.

questions.skill: Multiply, then add
questions.stem: A pencil costs 3 dollars and a notebook costs 9 dollars. Zane buys 6 pencils and 1 notebook. How many dollars does he pay?
questions.solution: Pencils: $6 \times 3 = 18$ dollars. Then $18 + 9 = 27$ dollars.

questions.skill: Add and subtract in two steps
questions.stem: Lena has 205 stamps. She gives 80 stamps to Jo and 45 stamps to Kay. How many stamps does Lena have left?
questions.solution: She gives away $80 + 45 = 125$ stamps. Then $205 - 125 = 80$ stamps are left.

questions.skill: Match a story and an equation
questions.stem: Which story matches $24 - 3 \times 5 = n$?
choices: A bag has 24 apples. 3 children each put in 5 apples.
A bag has 24 apples. 3 children take 5 apples in all.
A bag has 24 apples. 3 children each take 5 apples.
A bag has 24 apples. 3 children each take 5 apples, and then 2 more apples are put in.
questions.answer: A bag has 24 apples. 3 children each take 5 apples.
questions.solution: $3 \times 5$ is the apples 3 children each take. Taking them from 24 gives $24 - 3 \times 5$.

solve.answer: A bag has 24 apples. 3 children each take 5 apples.
solve.work: 24 minus 3 groups of 5 taken: 3 children each take 5.

questions.skill: Multiply, then subtract
questions.stem: A farm has 9 pens with 6 sheep in each pen. 15 sheep are sold at the market. How many sheep are left?
questions.solution: $9 \times 6 = 54$ sheep. Then $54 - 15 = 39$ sheep are left.

questions.skill: Two products, then combine
questions.stem: One box has 4 rows of 7 cookies. Another box has 3 rows of 6 cookies. How many more cookies are in the first box?
questions.solution: First box: $4 \times 7 = 28$. Second box: $3 \times 6 = 18$. The difference is $28 - 18 = 10$ cookies.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Pat had some stickers. She bought 4 packs of 6 stickers each, and now she has 51 stickers. How many stickers did Pat have at first?
questions.solution: The packs held $4 \times 6 = 24$ stickers. She had $51 - 24 = 27$ stickers at first.

questions.skill: Multiply, then subtract
questions.stem: A sticker sheet has 60 stickers. Ty puts 5 stickers on each of 8 cards. How many stickers are left on the sheet?
questions.solution: He uses $8 \times 5 = 40$ stickers. Then $60 - 40 = 20$ stickers are left.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Mr. Hall had some money. He spent 25 dollars on lunch and then earned 40 dollars. Now he has 90 dollars. How many dollars did he have at first?
questions.solution: Work backward. Before earning 40 he had $90 - 40 = 50$. Before spending 25 he had $50 + 25 = 75$ dollars.

questions.skill: Add and subtract in two steps
questions.stem: A school library has 148 books. It buys 76 new books and gives away 30 old books. How many books does the library have now?

questions.skill: Multiply, then add
questions.stem: Mr. Ruiz packs 8 boxes with 7 toys in each box. He then adds 9 more toys to the truck. How many toys are on the truck?
questions.solution: $8 \times 7 = 56$ toys in the boxes. Then $56 + 9 = 65$ toys.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: Pia has 6 red crayons and 5 blue crayons in a bag. She has 3 bags like that. She has $c$ crayons in all. Which equation matches the story?
questions.solution: Each bag has $6 + 5$ crayons, and there are 3 bags: $(6 + 5) \times 3 = c$.

solve.work: Each bag 6 + 5 crayons, 3 bags: (6 + 5) x 3 = c = 33.

questions.skill: Multiply, then add
questions.stem: Rhea swims 8 laps each day for 5 days. Then she swims 6 more laps on Saturday. How many laps does she swim in all?
questions.solution: In 5 days she swims $8 \times 5 = 40$ laps. Then $40 + 6 = 46$ laps.

questions.skill: Add, then multiply
questions.stem: A teacher buys 8 notebooks on Monday and 7 notebooks on Friday. Each notebook costs 4 dollars. How many dollars does she spend in all?
questions.solution: She buys $8 + 7 = 15$ notebooks. Then $15 \times 4 = 60$ dollars.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: Ravi had some stickers. He gave away 3 packs of 5 stickers and has 12 stickers left. Which equation can find $s$, the number of stickers Ravi had at first?
questions.solution: He started with $s$ and gave away $3 \times 5$ stickers, leaving 12: $s - 3 \times 5 = 12$.

solve.work: Start s, remove 3 packs of 5 = 15, left 12: s - 3x5 = 12 (s = 27).

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Neil had some dollars. He spent 6 dollars a day for 4 days. Now he has 17 dollars. How many dollars did Neil have at first?
questions.solution: He spent $4 \times 6 = 24$ dollars. He had $17 + 24 = 41$ dollars at first.

questions.skill: Add and subtract in two steps
questions.stem: A store had 85 hats. It sold 37 hats on Monday. Then 20 new hats arrived. How many hats does the store have now?

questions.skill: Add and subtract in two steps
questions.stem: A bus has 46 riders. 18 riders get off at the mall. Then 25 riders get on. How many riders are on the bus now?

questions.skill: Subtract, then multiply
questions.stem: A garden has 5 beds. Each bed has 9 plants, and 4 plants in each bed are tomatoes. The rest are peppers. How many pepper plants are in the garden?
questions.solution: Each bed has $9 - 4 = 5$ pepper plants. 5 beds have $5 \times 5 = 25$ pepper plants.

questions.skill: Two products, then combine
questions.stem: Amir made 6 cups with 5 beads in each cup. Bo made 4 cups with 8 beads in each cup. Which sentence is true?
choices: Amir has 2 more beads than Bo.
Bo has 2 more beads than Amir.
They have the same number of beads.
Bo has 6 more beads than Amir.
questions.answer: Bo has 2 more beads than Amir.
questions.solution: Amir has $6 \times 5 = 30$ beads. Bo has $4 \times 8 = 32$ beads. $32 - 30 = 2$, so Bo has 2 more.

solve.answer: Bo has 2 more beads than Amir.

questions.skill: Subtract, then multiply
questions.stem: Each box holds 12 pens. 4 pens in each box are red. There are 5 boxes. How many pens are not red?
questions.solution: Each box has $12 - 4 = 8$ pens that are not red. 5 boxes have $5 \times 8 = 40$ pens.

questions.skill: Compare, then combine
questions.stem: Sal has 28 marbles. Ted has 9 more marbles than Sal. Uma has 5 fewer marbles than Ted. How many marbles does Uma have?
questions.solution: Ted has $28 + 9 = 37$ marbles. Uma has $37 - 5 = 32$ marbles.

questions.skill: Two products, then combine
questions.stem: At the fair, Ella buys 6 tickets for rides at 4 dollars each and 3 tickets for games at 5 dollars each. How many dollars does she spend in all?
questions.solution: Rides: $6 \times 4 = 24$ dollars. Games: $3 \times 5 = 15$ dollars. Together $24 + 15 = 39$ dollars.

questions.skill: Compare, then combine
questions.stem: Lena collected 34 shells. Max collected 12 fewer shells than Lena. How many shells did they collect together?
questions.solution: Max collected $34 - 12 = 22$ shells. Together $34 + 22 = 56$ shells.

questions.skill: Multiply, then add
questions.stem: A stamp book has 8 pages with 9 stamps on each page. Nina adds 17 more stamps. How many stamps are in the book now?
questions.solution: The pages hold 8 x 9 = 72 stamps. Then 72 + 17 = 89.

questions.skill: Two products, then combine
questions.stem: A farmer picks 6 baskets of pears with 7 pears in each basket and 4 baskets of plums with 9 plums in each basket. How many pieces of fruit did he pick?
questions.solution: The pears: 6 x 7 = 42. The plums: 4 x 9 = 36. In all: 42 + 36 = 78.

questions.skill: Add and subtract in two steps
questions.stem: Omar has 250 stamps. He trades away 85 stamps and gets 120 new stamps in a swap. How many stamps does he have now?
questions.solution: After trading away 85: 250 - 85 = 165. After getting 120: 165 + 120 = 285.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: Ella buys 3 books that cost 7 dollars each and a pen that costs 2 dollars. She pays with a 50 dollar bill. Her change is c dollars. Which equation matches the story?
questions.solution: The books cost 3 x 7 dollars and the pen costs 2 dollars. Both are taken from 50, so 50 - 3 x 7 - 2 = c.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Mrs. Cho had some pencils. She gave 5 pencils to each of 4 students, and she has 9 pencils left. How many pencils did she have at first?
questions.solution: She gave away 4 x 5 = 20 pencils. She has 9 left, so she started with 20 + 9 = 29.

questions.skill: Multiply, then subtract
questions.stem: Lena has 9 bags with 6 beads in each bag. She uses 17 of the beads to make a bracelet. How many beads does she have left?
questions.solution: Lena has 9 x 6 = 54 beads. After using 17: 54 - 17 = 37.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Before lunch, a cafe had some muffins. It sold 18 muffins and then baked 24 more. Now it has 50 muffins. How many muffins did the cafe have before lunch?
questions.solution: Work backward. Before baking 24 more, it had 50 - 24 = 26. Before selling 18, it had 26 + 18 = 44.

questions.skill: Add, then multiply
questions.stem: Mrs. Reed makes 4 necklaces. Each necklace has 7 red beads and 8 green beads. How many beads does she use in all?
questions.solution: Each necklace has 7 + 8 = 15 beads. For 4 necklaces: 4 x 15 = 60 beads.

questions.skill: Two products, then combine
questions.stem: A baker makes 7 trays of 8 cookies. She sells 5 bags of 6 cookies. How many cookies are not sold?
questions.solution: She makes 7 x 8 = 56 cookies and sells 5 x 6 = 30. Then 56 - 30 = 26.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: Which story matches the equation $3 \times 6 + 4 = n$?
choices: Sam has 3 packs of 6 cards and gives away 4 cards.
Sam has 3 packs of 6 cards and gets 4 more cards.
Sam has 3 packs of 4 cards and gets 6 more cards.
Sam has 3 cards and 6 cards and gets 4 more cards.
questions.answer: Sam has 3 packs of 6 cards and gets 4 more cards.
questions.solution: 3 x 6 means 3 packs of 6 cards, and + 4 means 4 more cards are added.

solve.answer: Sam has 3 packs of 6 cards and gets 4 more cards.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: Mia reads 9 pages each day for 5 days. She has 12 pages left in her book. The book has $p$ pages in all. Which equation matches the story?
questions.solution: She has read $9 \times 5$ pages and has 12 left, so the whole book is $9 \times 5 + 12 = p$.

solve.work: 9 pages x 5 days = 45 read, plus 12 left: p = 45 + 12.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Jenna had 90 dollars. She spent some dollars at the store and then earned 15 dollars. Now she has 70 dollars. How many dollars did she spend?
questions.solution: Before earning 15 she had $70 - 15 = 55$ dollars. She spent $90 - 55 = 35$ dollars.

questions.skill: Multiply, then add
questions.stem: Each ticket to a play costs 6 dollars. A family buys 7 tickets and a program for 5 dollars. How many dollars do they pay?
questions.solution: Tickets: $7 \times 6 = 42$ dollars. Then $42 + 5 = 47$ dollars.

questions.skill: Two products, then combine
questions.stem: A bakery sells 7 boxes with 9 muffins in each box and 6 boxes with 8 cupcakes in each box. How many muffins and cupcakes does the bakery sell in all?
questions.solution: Muffins: $7 \times 9 = 63$. Cupcakes: $6 \times 8 = 48$. Together $63 + 48 = 111$.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Omar has 8 boxes with 6 stickers in each box. He gives some stickers to friends and has 31 stickers left. How many stickers did he give away?
questions.solution: He had $8 \times 6 = 48$ stickers. He gave away $48 - 31 = 17$ stickers.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: Cal has 5 boxes with 7 toy cars in each box and some loose toy cars. He has 41 toy cars in all. Which equation can find $l$, the number of loose toy cars?
questions.solution: The boxes hold $5 \times 7$ cars. Adding the $l$ loose cars gives all 41: $5 \times 7 + l = 41$.

questions.skill: Subtract, then multiply
questions.stem: A tray holds 15 muffins. 6 muffins on each tray are burnt. A baker has 4 trays. How many muffins are not burnt?
questions.solution: Each tray has $15 - 6 = 9$ muffins that are not burnt. 4 trays have $4 \times 9 = 36$ muffins.

solve.work: Not burnt per tray: 15 - 6 = 9. Four trays: 9 x 4 = 36.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Kim saves 7 dollars each week for 6 weeks. Then she spends some dollars and has 15 dollars left. How many dollars did she spend?
questions.solution: She saves $7 \times 6 = 42$ dollars. She spends $42 - 15 = 27$ dollars.

questions.skill: Multiply, then subtract
questions.stem: A school has 8 vans. Each van has 9 seats. There are 65 students going on the trip. How many seats are empty?
questions.solution: There are $8 \times 9 = 72$ seats. Then $72 - 65 = 7$ seats are empty.

questions.skill: Multiply, then compare
questions.stem: Sam has 3 packs with 9 cards in each pack. Tia has 8 fewer cards than Sam. How many cards does Tia have?
questions.solution: Sam has $3 \times 9 = 27$ cards. Tia has $27 - 8 = 19$ cards.

questions.skill: Multiply, then add
questions.stem: A theater has 9 rows with 8 seats in each row. It adds 24 folding chairs. How many seats does the theater have now?
questions.solution: $9 \times 8 = 72$ seats. Then $72 + 24 = 96$ seats.

questions.skill: Two products, then combine
questions.stem: A school buys 9 boxes with 4 pens in each box and 6 boxes with 3 pens in each box. How many more pens are in the first group of boxes than in the second?
questions.solution: First group: $9 \times 4 = 36$. Second group: $6 \times 3 = 18$. The difference is $36 - 18 = 18$ pens.

questions.skill: Two products, then combine
questions.stem: Rin buys 3 packs with 9 pencils in each pack and 2 packs with 8 erasers in each pack. How many pencils and erasers does she buy in all?
questions.solution: Pencils: $3 \times 9 = 27$. Erasers: $2 \times 8 = 16$. Together $27 + 16 = 43$.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: Hana had some beads. She gave away 14 beads and then found 9 beads. Now she has 36 beads. Which equation can find $b$, the number of beads Hana had at first?
questions.solution: She started with $b$, lost 14 and gained 9: $b - 14 + 9 = 36$.

solve.work: Start b, give away 14 (subtract), find 9 (add): b - 14 + 9 = 36, b = 41.

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Mr. Webb had some dollars. He bought 3 hats for 12 dollars each, and then he had 29 dollars left. How many dollars did Mr. Webb have at first?
questions.solution: The hats cost $3 \times 12 = 36$ dollars. He had $36 + 29 = 65$ dollars at first.

questions.skill: Add and subtract in two steps
questions.stem: A pool has 120 swimmers in the morning. 45 swimmers leave at noon and 70 more swimmers come in the afternoon. How many swimmers are in the pool then?

questions.skill: Add and subtract in two steps
questions.stem: A school collected 342 cans in May and 275 cans in June. It then gave 150 cans to a recycling center. How many cans does the school have left?

questions.skill: Find the unknown by working backward
questions.stem: Zed had some dollars. He bought 3 games for 8 dollars each. Now he has 25 dollars. How many dollars did Zed have at first?
questions.solution: The games cost $3 \times 8 = 24$ dollars. He had $24 + 25 = 49$ dollars at first.

questions.skill: Add, then multiply
questions.stem: At a party, 12 children and 8 adults each get 3 balloons. How many balloons are needed?
questions.solution: There are $12 + 8 = 20$ people. Then $20 \times 3 = 60$ balloons.

questions.skill: Match a story and an equation
questions.stem: Which story matches $(5 + 4) \times 3 = n$?
choices: There are 5 baskets with 4 pears in each basket, and 3 more apples.
There are 5 apples and 4 pears in each of 3 baskets.
There are 5 apples, 4 pears and 3 plums.
There are 3 baskets with 5 apples in each basket, and 4 are eaten.
questions.answer: There are 5 apples and 4 pears in each of 3 baskets.
questions.solution: $5 + 4$ is the fruit in one basket and $\times 3$ is for 3 baskets. So each of 3 baskets holds 5 apples and 4 pears.

solve.answer: There are 5 apples and 4 pears in each of 3 baskets.
solve.work: (5+4)x3: 9 fruits in each of 3 baskets = 5 apples and 4 pears in each of 3 baskets.

questions.skill: Multiply, then subtract
questions.stem: A farmer plants 7 rows with 8 seeds in each row. A bird eats 13 of the seeds. How many seeds are left?
questions.solution: $7 \times 8 = 56$ seeds. Then $56 - 13 = 43$ seeds are left.

questions.skill: Compare, then combine
questions.stem: Tara has 25 stickers. Ned has 8 fewer stickers than Tara. How many stickers do the two of them have together?
questions.solution: Ned has $25 - 8 = 17$ stickers. Together $25 + 17 = 42$ stickers.

questions.skill: Write an equation with an unknown
questions.stem: Lia has 14 shells. Max has 6 more shells than Lia. Together they have $s$ shells. Which equation matches the story?
questions.solution: Max has $14 + 6$ shells. Together: $14 + (14 + 6) = s$, which is $14 + 14 + 6 = s$.

questions.skill: Skip counting patterns
questions.stem: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, ... What number comes next?
questions.solution: Each number is 5 more than the one before. 20 + 5 = 25.

questions.skill: Multiples of 5 and 10 end in 0 or 5
questions.stem: Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, ... Every number you say ends in the same digit. Which digit?
questions.solution: Counting by 10s adds one more ten each time, so the ones digit stays 0.

questions.skill: Even and odd products and sums
questions.stem: Which product is an even number?
questions.solution: $4 \times 7 = 28$, which is even. The other products, 15, 21 and 45, are all odd, because an odd number times an odd number is odd.

questions.skill: Doubles patterns in the multiplication table
questions.stem: In a multiplication table, the 4s row is double the 2s row. Since $2 \times 6 = 12$, what is $4 \times 6$?
questions.solution: Double 12 is 24, so $4 \times 6 = 24$.

questions.skill: Hundreds board rows and columns
questions.stem: A hundreds board has the numbers 1 to 100 in rows of 10. Dev is on 34 and moves down one row. What number is he on now?
questions.solution: Moving down one row on a hundreds board adds 10. 34 + 10 = 44.

questions.skill: Rows, columns and symmetry of the multiplication table
questions.stem: In a multiplication table, $3 \times 8$ and $8 \times 3$ are in different places but show the same product. If $3 \times 8 = 24$, what is $8 \times 3$?
questions.solution: Changing the order of the factors does not change the product, so $8 \times 3 = 24$.

solve.work: Order of factors does not change the product: 8 x 3 = 24.

questions.skill: Skip counting patterns
questions.stem: Count by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, ... Which number is also in this pattern?
questions.solution: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 12 + 3 = 15. The numbers 14, 16 and 17 are not in the pattern.

solve.work: Multiples of 3: 12, 15, 18. 15 is in the list; 14, 16, 17 are not.

questions.skill: Patterns in the 9s
questions.stem: Look at the 9s: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45. The tens digit goes up by 1 each time, and the two digits of each number add to 9. What is the next number?
questions.solution: The next number is 45 + 9 = 54. Check the pattern: the tens digit is 5 and $5 + 4 = 9$.

solve.work: After 45 the tens digit becomes 5 and digits add to 9: 54 (= 9 x 6).

questions.skill: Rows, columns and symmetry of the multiplication table
questions.stem: The column for 7s in a multiplication table has the products 7, 14, 21, 28, ... How much more is each product than the one above it?
questions.solution: Each step down adds one more 7, so each product is 7 more than the one above it.

questions.skill: Multiples of 5 and 10 end in 0 or 5
questions.stem: Which number is a multiple of 5?
questions.solution: 65 ends in a 5, and every multiple of 5 ends in 0 or 5. Also $5 \times 13 = 65$.

questions.solution: $8 \times 5 = 40$, so 8 groups of 5 tens is 40 tens, which is 400.

questions.skill: Equal groups word problem
questions.stem: A library has 9 shelves. Each shelf holds 40 books. How many books are on the shelves in all?
questions.solution: $9 \times 4 = 36$, so 9 shelves of 4 tens is 36 tens, which is 360 books.

questions.skill: Properties: break apart and regroup factors
questions.stem: Jon thinks of $4 \times 60$ as $(4 \times 6) \times 10$. What is $4 \times 60$?
questions.solution: $4 \times 6 = 24$, and then $24 \times 10 = 240$.

questions.skill: Find the missing factor
questions.stem: What number makes this true? $5 \times ? = 200$
questions.solution: 200 is 20 tens. 5 times 4 tens is 20 tens, so the ? is 40. Check: $5 \times 40 = 200$.

questions.skill: Think of the multiple of 10 as tens
questions.stem: Which number is 15 tens?
questions.solution: 1 ten is 10, so 15 tens is $15 \times 10 = 150$.

questions.skill: Cost and savings with equal amounts
questions.stem: Seven friends each save 30 dollars. How many dollars do they save in all?
questions.solution: $7 \times 3 = 21$, so 7 groups of 3 tens is 21 tens, which is 210 dollars.

questions.skill: Compare products
questions.stem: Which product is the greatest?
questions.solution: $5 \times 50 = 250$. The others are $4 \times 60 = 240$, $6 \times 40 = 240$ and $8 \times 30 = 240$.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle with a multiple of 10
questions.stem: A rectangle is 8 units wide and 20 units long. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: Area is width times length. $8 \times 20$ is 8 groups of 2 tens, which is 16 tens, or 160.

questions.skill: Properties: break apart and regroup factors
questions.stem: Which is equal to $9 \times 20$?
questions.solution: $9 \times 20 = 9 \times 2 \times 10 = 18 \times 10 = 180$. The other choices are 18, 1,800 and 1,800.

questions.skill: Multiply by the largest multiples of 10
questions.stem: What is $9 \times 90$?
questions.solution: $9 \times 9 = 81$, so 9 groups of 9 tens is 81 tens, which is 810.

questions.skill: Two-step problems
questions.stem: Dan buys 6 packs of 30 stickers. He then gives 50 stickers away. How many stickers does he have left?
questions.solution: $6 \times 30 = 180$ stickers. Then $180 - 50 = 130$.

questions.skill: Find the missing factor
questions.stem: What number makes this true? $? \times 70 = 560$
questions.solution: 560 is 56 tens. Since $8 \times 7 = 56$, the ? is 8. Check: $8 \times 70 = 560$.

questions.skill: Check which product is correct
questions.stem: Which equation is NOT true?
questions.solution: $5 \times 30 = 150$, not 160. The other three equal 160: $2 \times 8 = 16$, $4 \times 4 = 16$ and $8 \times 2 = 16$ tens.

questions.skill: Two-step problems
questions.stem: A theater has 8 rows of 30 seats and 3 rows of 20 seats. How many seats does it have in all?

questions.skill: Think of the multiple of 10 as tens
questions.stem: Which statement about $6 \times 50$ is true?
questions.solution: 6 groups of 5 tens is $6 \times 5 = 30$ tens. 30 tens is 300.

questions.skill: Two-step problems
questions.stem: A teacher has 5 boxes of 60 crayons and 4 boxes of 90 crayons. How many more crayons are in the 4 boxes than in the 5 boxes?

questions.skill: Two-step problems
questions.stem: Nia has 3 bags of 70 beads. Eli has 2 bags of 90 beads. Who has more beads, and how many more?
questions.solution: Nia has $3 \times 70 = 210$ beads. Eli has $2 \times 90 = 180$ beads. Nia has 210 - 180 = 30 more.

solve.work: Nia 3 x 70 = 210, Eli 2 x 90 = 180; Nia has 30 more.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle with a multiple of 10
questions.stem: A rectangle is 6 units wide and 70 units long. It is cut into two parts. One part is 6 units by 40 units. What is the area of the other part in square units?
questions.solution: The whole rectangle has area $6 \times 70 = 420$. The 6-by-40 part has area $6 \times 40 = 240$. The other part is $420 - 240 = 180$.

questions.skill: Properties: break apart and regroup factors
questions.stem: Which has the same product as $3 \times 60$?
questions.solution: $3 \times 60 = 180$ and $6 \times 30 = 180$. The others are 60, 160 and 150.

questions.skill: Name the unit fraction for one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. Ben eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza does he eat? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: The pizza is cut into 4 equal parts, and Ben eats 1 of them. One of 4 equal parts is $\frac{1}{4}$.

solve.work: 4 equal slices, 1 eaten: 1 of 4 equal parts = 1/4.

questions.skill: Name the unit fraction for one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A ribbon is cut into 3 equal pieces. What fraction of the ribbon is one piece?
questions.solution: The ribbon is cut into 3 equal pieces, so one piece is $\frac{1}{3}$ of the ribbon.

solve.work: 3 equal pieces; one piece is 1 of 3 equal parts = 1/3.

questions.skill: Find the number of equal parts from a unit fraction
questions.stem: A rectangle is cut into equal parts. One part is $\frac{1}{6}$ of the rectangle. How many equal parts is the rectangle cut into?
questions.solution: The denominator 6 tells how many equal parts make the whole. The rectangle is cut into 6 equal parts.

solve.work: A unit fraction 1/6 means the whole is cut into 6 equal parts.

questions.skill: Meaning of the numerator and denominator of a unit fraction
questions.stem: In the fraction $\frac{1}{8}$, what does the 8 tell you?
choices: The whole is exactly 8 units long
There are 8 parts that are shaded
The whole is cut into 8 equal parts
Each of the parts is 8 units long
questions.answer: The whole is cut into 8 equal parts
questions.solution: The bottom number, the denominator, tells how many equal parts the whole is cut into. In $\frac{1}{8}$ it is cut into 8 equal parts.

solve.answer: The whole is cut into 8 equal parts
solve.work: The denominator 8 tells how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

questions.skill: Unit fractions on a length or number-line model
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 8 equal lengths. What fraction is at the first mark to the right of 0? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: Each of the 8 equal lengths is $\frac{1}{8}$ long. The first mark to the right of 0 is one length from 0, so it is at $\frac{1}{8}$.

solve.work: 8 equal lengths from 0 to 1; the first mark is one of eight lengths from 0: 1/8.

questions.skill: Name the unit fraction for one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A whole is cut into 6 equal parts. What is one part called?
questions.solution: A whole cut into 6 equal parts has parts called sixths. One part is one sixth, $\frac{1}{6}$.

solve.work: One of 6 equal parts is one sixth.

questions.skill: Parts must be equal to make a unit fraction
questions.stem: A square is cut into 2 parts. Which fact must be true for each part to be $\frac{1}{2}$ of the square?
choices: The two parts are the same size
One part is bigger than the other
The two parts are both squares
The two parts are both triangles
questions.answer: The two parts are the same size
questions.solution: Halves are 2 EQUAL parts of a whole. Each part is $\frac{1}{2}$ only when the two parts are the same size.

solve.answer: The two parts are the same size
solve.work: Each part is 1/2 only if the 2 parts are equal in size (shape need not match a particular kind).

questions.skill: Name the unit fraction for one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: Lena shares a sandwich equally with 1 friend, so the two of them get the same amount. What fraction of the sandwich does Lena get? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: The sandwich is shared into 2 equal parts, and Lena gets 1 of them. That is $\frac{1}{2}$ of the sandwich.

solve.work: Shared equally between 2 people: each gets 1 of 2 equal parts = 1/2.

questions.skill: Unit fractions on a length or number-line model
questions.stem: A string 1 yard long is cut into 6 equal pieces. What fraction of a yard is each piece? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: One yard is cut into 6 equal pieces, so each piece is $\frac{1}{6}$ of a yard.

solve.work: 1 yard into 6 equal pieces: each is 1/6 yard.

questions.skill: Meaning of the numerator and denominator of a unit fraction
questions.stem: Which of these is a unit fraction?
questions.solution: A unit fraction has 1 on top, because it is one equal part of a whole. Only $\frac{1}{3}$ has 1 as its numerator.

questions.skill: Size of unit fractions: more equal parts, smaller parts
questions.stem: The pizzas are all the same size. Which slice is the largest?
questions.solution: When the whole is the same, cutting it into fewer equal parts makes bigger parts. Halves are the biggest of these, so $\frac{1}{2}$ of a pizza is the largest slice.

solve.work: Same-size wholes: fewer equal parts gives bigger parts; 1/2 > 1/3 > 1/6 > 1/8.

questions.skill: Build a fraction from unit fractions
questions.stem: A strip is cut into 8 equal parts. Tia colors 3 of the parts. Each part is $\frac{1}{8}$ of the strip. What fraction of the strip does Tia color? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: Tia colors 3 parts, and each part is $\frac{1}{8}$. So she colors $\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{3}{8}$ of the strip.

questions.skill: Parts must be equal to make a unit fraction
questions.stem: A 12-inch strip of paper is cut into 3 pieces. Which cut makes each piece $\frac{1}{3}$ of the strip?
choices: Pieces 6 inches, 3 inches and 3 inches long
Pieces 5 inches, 5 inches and 2 inches long
Pieces 8 inches, 2 inches and 2 inches long
Pieces 4 inches, 4 inches and 4 inches long
questions.answer: Pieces 4 inches, 4 inches and 4 inches long
questions.solution: Thirds are 3 EQUAL pieces. $12 \div 3 = 4$, so each piece must be 4 inches long.

solve.answer: Pieces 4 inches, 4 inches and 4 inches long
solve.work: Equal thirds of 12 inches are 12/3 = 4 inches each: 4, 4, 4.

questions.skill: Unit fractions on a length or number-line model
questions.stem: Sam hops along a number line from 0 to 1. Each hop is $\frac{1}{4}$ long, and he lands exactly on 1 at the end. How many hops does he take?
questions.solution: Four hops of $\frac{1}{4}$ make $\frac{4}{4}$, which is 1 whole. Sam takes 4 hops.

solve.work: From 0 to 1 in hops of 1/4: 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4 = 1, so 4 hops.

questions.skill: Meaning of the numerator and denominator of a unit fraction
questions.stem: What does the 1 in $\frac{1}{3}$ tell you?
choices: It counts 1 of the equal parts
The whole is cut into just 1 part
There is only 1 whole in the problem
questions.answer: It counts 1 of the equal parts
questions.solution: The top number, the numerator, tells how many of the equal parts we are talking about. In $\frac{1}{3}$ it is 1 part out of 3 equal parts.

solve.answer: It counts 1 of the equal parts
solve.work: The numerator 1 counts one of the equal parts.

questions.skill: Use a unit fraction to find a part or the whole
questions.stem: A rectangle is made of 8 small squares that are all the same size. It is cut into 4 equal parts. How many small squares are in one part?
questions.solution: Each part is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the rectangle. 8 squares shared into 4 equal parts is $8 \div 4 = 2$ squares in each part.

solve.work: 8 equal small squares into 4 equal parts: 8/4 = 2 squares each.

questions.skill: Name the unit fraction for one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A square is cut into 8 equal parts. Zoe shades 1 part. Which fraction names the shaded part?
questions.solution: The square has 8 equal parts and 1 is shaded. The shaded part is $\frac{1}{8}$ of the square.

questions.skill: Unit fractions on a length or number-line model
questions.stem: The marks on a number line from 0 to 1 are equally spaced. The first mark to the right of 0 is at $\frac{1}{3}$. How many equal spaces are there between 0 and 1?
questions.solution: The first mark is at $\frac{1}{3}$, so each space is $\frac{1}{3}$ long. It takes 3 of them to get from 0 to 1.

solve.work: First mark at 1/3 means each space is 1/3, so 3 equal spaces between 0 and 1.

questions.skill: Size of unit fractions: more equal parts, smaller parts
questions.stem: Nina and Omar have candy bars of the same length. Nina cuts hers into 3 equal pieces. Omar cuts his into 6 equal pieces. Which statement is true?
choices: Omar’s pieces are longer than Nina’s pieces
Omar’s pieces are the same length as Nina’s pieces
Omar’s pieces are shorter than Nina’s pieces
Omar’s pieces are twice as long as Nina’s pieces
questions.answer: Omar’s pieces are shorter than Nina’s pieces
questions.solution: The bars are the same length. The more equal pieces a bar is cut into, the shorter each piece is. Sixths are shorter than thirds.

solve.answer: Omar’s pieces are shorter than Nina’s pieces
solve.work: Same length: 6 equal pieces are smaller than 3 equal pieces (1/6 < 1/3); Omar’s are half as long, so shorter.

questions.skill: Use a unit fraction to find a part or the whole
questions.stem: A 12-centimeter ribbon is cut into 3 equal pieces. Each piece is $\frac{1}{3}$ of the ribbon. How many centimeters long is each piece?
questions.solution: One third of 12 centimeters is $12 \div 3 = 4$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Size of unit fractions: more equal parts, smaller parts
questions.stem: Jada says $\frac{1}{8}$ of a pizza is bigger than $\frac{1}{4}$ of the same pizza because 8 is bigger than 4. Which sentence explains her mistake?
choices: More equal parts mean each part is bigger
A pizza cannot be cut into 8 equal parts
Unit fractions are always the same size
More equal parts make each part smaller
questions.answer: More equal parts make each part smaller
questions.solution: The pizza is the same size each time. Cutting it into 8 equal slices gives smaller slices than cutting it into 4. So $\frac{1}{8}$ is smaller than $\frac{1}{4}$.

solve.answer: More equal parts make each part smaller
solve.work: Cutting the same pizza into more equal parts makes each part smaller, so 1/8 < 1/4.

questions.skill: Use a unit fraction to find a part or the whole
questions.stem: A ribbon is cut into 4 equal pieces. One piece is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the whole ribbon and is 5 inches long. How many inches long is the whole ribbon?
questions.solution: The whole ribbon is 4 pieces of 5 inches. $4 \times 5 = 20$ inches.

solve.work: 4 equal pieces each 5 inches: 4 x 5 = 20 inches.

questions.skill: Parts must be equal to make a unit fraction
questions.stem: A square cake is made of 16 small squares that are all the same size. It is cut into 4 pieces. Which cut makes each piece $\frac{1}{4}$ of the cake?
questions.solution: Fourths are 4 EQUAL pieces. $16 \div 4 = 4$, so each piece must have 4 small squares.

solve.work: 16 squares into 4 equal pieces: 16/4 = 4 each; only 4,4,4,4 is equal.

questions.skill: Build a fraction from unit fractions
questions.stem: A rectangle is cut into 8 equal parts. Mark shades 3 of the parts and Lia shades 2 other parts. Together, what fraction of the rectangle did they shade? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: Each part is $\frac{1}{8}$ of the rectangle. They shaded $3 + 2 = 5$ parts, which is $\frac{5}{8}$ of the rectangle.

questions.skill: Build a fraction from unit fractions
questions.stem: Which sum of unit fractions equals 1 whole?
questions.solution: It takes 6 sixths to make 1 whole. Six terms of $\frac{1}{6}$ add up to $\frac{6}{6} = 1$.

solve.work: Six sixths make 1 whole: the option with six terms of 1/6 (others have 5, 7, 8 terms).

questions.skill: Unit fractions on a length or number-line model
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 3 equal lengths. Amir starts at 0 and makes 2 hops, each one length long. What fraction is he at? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: Each length is $\frac{1}{3}$. After 2 hops he has gone $\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$.

solve.work: Each length is 1/3; 2 hops from 0 reach 2/3.

questions.skill: Use a unit fraction to find a part or the whole
questions.stem: Mia and Sam each eat $\frac{1}{4}$ of their own pizza. Mia’s pizza is large and Sam’s pizza is small. Which statement is true?
choices: Sam eats more pizza than Mia
They eat the same amount of pizza
Mia eats more pizza than Sam
questions.answer: Mia eats more pizza than Sam
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{4}$ of a large whole is more than $\frac{1}{4}$ of a small whole. A fraction only compares well when the wholes are the same size.

solve.answer: Mia eats more pizza than Sam
solve.work: A fraction depends on the size of the whole: 1/4 of a large pizza is more than 1/4 of a small one, so Mia eats more.

questions.skill: Name the unit fraction for one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A 24-inch strip is cut into equal pieces that are each 3 inches long. Each piece is what unit fraction of the strip? Write your answer as a fraction.
questions.solution: $24 \div 3 = 8$, so the strip is cut into 8 equal pieces. Each piece is $\frac{1}{8}$ of the strip.

solve.work: 24/3 = 8 pieces, so each piece is 1/8 of the strip.

questions.skill: Parts must be equal to make a unit fraction
questions.stem: Ella cuts a square sandwich from one corner to the opposite corner. This makes 2 triangles that are the same size. She says each triangle is $\frac{1}{2}$ of the sandwich. Is she right?
choices: No, because halves must be rectangles
No, because a half cannot be a triangle
No, because the cut is not straight across
Yes, because the 2 parts are equal in size
questions.answer: Yes, because the 2 parts are equal in size
questions.solution: A half is one of 2 EQUAL parts. The shape of the parts does not matter, so two equal triangles are halves.

solve.answer: Yes, because the 2 parts are equal in size
solve.work: Two equal-size parts of a whole are halves, whatever their shape: Yes.

questions.skill: Size of unit fractions: more equal parts, smaller parts
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into equal slices, and the number of slices is 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8. Each slice is bigger than $\frac{1}{8}$ of the pizza and smaller than $\frac{1}{4}$ of the pizza. How many slices is the pizza cut into?
questions.solution: A slice bigger than $\frac{1}{8}$ and smaller than $\frac{1}{4}$ comes from fewer than 8 and more than 4 parts. Of 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8, only 6 fits, so each slice is $\frac{1}{6}$.

solve.work: Allowed slice counts 2,3,4,6,8; need 1/8 < 1/n < 1/4, i.e. 4 < n < 8: n = 6 only.

questions.skill: Name the fraction shaded on an area model
questions.stem: A rectangle is cut into 4 equal parts. 3 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
questions.solution: There are 4 equal parts and 3 are shaded. The shaded part is 3/4 of the rectangle.

questions.skill: A unit fraction is one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Each slice is what fraction of the whole pizza?
questions.solution: The whole is cut into 8 equal parts, so each part is the unit fraction 1/8.

questions.skill: A fraction is a count of unit fractions
questions.stem: How many pieces of size $\frac{1}{3}$ are put together to make $\frac{2}{3}$?
questions.solution: 2/3 is 2 copies of the unit fraction 1/3.

questions.skill: Make a fraction on a number line by equal jumps from 0
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 4 equal parts. Ben starts at 0 and jumps 1 part. Where does he land?
questions.solution: Each part is 1/4 long. One jump from 0 lands at 1/4.

solve.work: One jump of 1/4 from 0 lands at 1/4.

questions.skill: A unit fraction is one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A garden is split into 6 equal beds. 1 bed has tomatoes. What fraction of the garden has tomatoes?
questions.solution: The garden has 6 equal beds, so 1 bed is the unit fraction 1/6.

questions.skill: A unit fraction is one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 6 equal parts. What fraction names the length of one part?
questions.solution: The whole length 1 is cut into 6 equal parts, so each part is 1/6 long.

solve.work: Each of 6 equal parts of 0 to 1 is 1/6 long.

questions.skill: A fraction is a count of unit fractions
questions.stem: Count by unit fractions: $\frac{1}{8}$, $\frac{2}{8}$, $\frac{3}{8}$. What fraction comes next?
questions.solution: Each step adds one more 1/8. After 3/8 comes 4/8.

questions.skill: Name the fraction shaded on an area model
questions.stem: A square is cut into 6 equal parts. 4 of the parts are shaded. Which fraction names the shaded part?
questions.solution: 4 of the 6 equal parts are shaded, so the shaded part is 4/6.

questions.skill: A unit fraction is one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: A circle is cut into equal parts. Each part is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the circle. How many equal parts is the circle cut into?
questions.solution: The bottom number of the unit fraction 1/4 tells how many equal parts make the whole. There are 4 parts.

questions.skill: A fraction is a count of unit fractions
questions.stem: Which fraction is 3 copies of $\frac{1}{6}$ put together?
questions.solution: Each copy is 1/6. Three copies make 3/6.

questions.skill: Name the fraction shaded on an area model
questions.stem: A rectangle is cut into 8 equal parts. 5 parts are shaded and 3 parts are not shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?
questions.solution: There are 8 equal parts in all. 5 of them are shaded, so the shaded part is 5/8.

questions.skill: Make a fraction on a number line by equal jumps from 0
questions.stem: On a number line from 0 to 1 cut into 6 equal parts, Mia starts at 0 and makes 4 jumps of $\frac{1}{6}$. Where does she land?
questions.solution: Each jump is 1/6. Four jumps of 1/6 land at 4/6.

questions.skill: Name the fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 4 equal parts. Point A is at the 3rd mark to the right of 0. What fraction names point A?
questions.solution: Each mark is one more 1/4 from 0. The 3rd mark is at 3/4.

solve.work: Marks at 0, 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 1; the 3rd mark right of 0 is 3/4.

questions.skill: A fraction is a count of unit fractions
questions.stem: Dan says that $\frac{5}{6}$ is made of 5 copies of one unit fraction. Which unit fraction is it?
questions.solution: The bottom number 6 tells the size of each part. 5/6 is 5 copies of 1/6.

questions.skill: The whole as a fraction (b/b) and parts left to make it
questions.stem: A whole is cut into 3 equal parts, and all 3 parts are shaded. What fraction is shaded? Write it with 3 as the bottom number.
questions.solution: All 3 of the 3 equal parts make the whole. The shaded fraction is 3/3, which is the same as 1.

questions.skill: Name the fraction shaded on an area model
questions.stem: Which sentence describes $\frac{2}{3}$ of a rectangle?
choices: The rectangle is cut into 3 equal parts, and 1 is shaded.
The rectangle is cut into 5 equal parts, and 2 are shaded.
The rectangle is cut into 3 equal parts, and 2 are shaded.
The rectangle is cut into 3 unequal parts, and 2 are shaded.
questions.answer: The rectangle is cut into 3 equal parts, and 2 are shaded.
questions.solution: The bottom number 3 is the number of equal parts, and the top number 2 is the number of parts shaded.

solve.answer: The rectangle is cut into 3 equal parts, and 2 are shaded.

questions.skill: Make a fraction on a number line by equal jumps from 0
questions.stem: On a number line from 0 to 1, each equal part is $\frac{1}{8}$ long. Starting at 0, how many jumps of $\frac{1}{8}$ does it take to land on $\frac{6}{8}$?
questions.solution: Each jump adds 1/8. It takes 6 jumps to reach 6/8.

questions.skill: Name the fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 6 equal parts. Point B is 2 parts to the left of 1. Which fraction names point B?
questions.solution: 1 is at 6/6. Moving 2 parts to the left gives 6/6 - 2/6 = 4/6.

questions.skill: A fraction is a count of unit fractions
questions.stem: Tom colors $\frac{1}{8}$ of a strip, then $\frac{1}{8}$ more, then $\frac{1}{8}$ more. What fraction of the strip has he colored?
questions.solution: He colored 3 pieces that are each 1/8. That is 3/8 of the strip.

questions.skill: The whole as a fraction (b/b) and parts left to make it
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into fourths. Which fraction is at the same point as 1?
questions.solution: The 4th jump of 1/4 lands on 1. So 4/4 is the same point as 1.

questions.skill: A unit fraction is one equal part of a whole
