questions.stem: A rectangle is cut into equal parts, and 3 shaded parts make $\frac{3}{8}$ of the rectangle. How many equal parts is the rectangle cut into?
questions.solution: The bottom number of 3/8 is the number of equal parts in the whole. So there are 8 parts.

solve.work: 3 parts are 3/8, so each part is 1/8: 8 parts.

questions.skill: Make a fraction on a number line by equal jumps from 0
questions.stem: Pat lands on $\frac{5}{6}$ by making jumps from 0, and every jump is a unit fraction. Which describes her jumps?
questions.solution: 5/6 is 5 copies of 1/6, so Pat makes 5 jumps and each is 1/6 long.

questions.skill: Name the fraction at a point on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 8 equal parts. Point C is 3 parts to the left of the point 1. What fraction names point C?
questions.solution: 1 is the same as 8/8. 3 parts to the left is 8/8 - 3/8 = 5/8.

questions.skill: The whole as a fraction (b/b) and parts left to make it
questions.stem: Beth has colored $\frac{5}{8}$ of a banner. She colors more $\frac{1}{8}$ pieces until the whole banner is colored. How many more $\frac{1}{8}$ pieces does she color?
questions.solution: The whole banner is 8/8. She has 5/8, so she needs 8 - 5 = 3 more pieces of 1/8.

questions.skill: A fraction is a count of unit fractions
questions.stem: A rectangle is cut into 6 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded. Which statement is true?
choices: The shaded part is 5 copies of $\frac{1}{5}$.
The shaded part is 6 copies of $\frac{1}{5}$.
The shaded part is 5 copies of $\frac{1}{6}$.
The shaded part is 1 copy of $\frac{1}{6}$.
questions.answer: The shaded part is 5 copies of $\frac{1}{6}$.
questions.solution: Each equal part is 1/6, and 5 parts are shaded, so the shaded part is 5 copies of 1/6.

solve.answer: The shaded part is 5 copies of $\frac{1}{6}$.

questions.skill: The whole as a fraction (b/b) and parts left to make it
questions.stem: On a number line, 3 jumps of the same size from 0 land at $\frac{3}{4}$. How many more jumps of that size are needed to reach 1?
questions.solution: Each jump is 1/4. 1 is the same as 4/4, so 4 - 3 = 1 more jump is needed.

solve.work: Each jump 1/4; 3/4 to 4/4 needs 1 more jump.

questions.skill: Make a fraction on a number line by equal jumps from 0
questions.stem: Which list of marks cuts a number line from 0 to 1 into equal fourths?
questions.solution: Fourths need 4 equal parts. The marks 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 sit between 0 and 1.

questions.skill: Name the fraction shaded on an area model
questions.stem: A square is cut into 8 equal parts. 3 parts are shaded blue and 2 parts are shaded red. What fraction of the square is shaded in all?
questions.solution: 3 + 2 = 5 parts are shaded out of 8 equal parts. The shaded fraction is 5/8.

questions.skill: A unit fraction is one equal part of a whole
questions.stem: Which statement is true when a number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 3 equal parts?
choices: Each part is $\frac{1}{3}$ long, and 2 parts reach 1.
Each part is $\frac{1}{2}$ long, and 3 parts reach 1.
Each part is $\frac{1}{3}$ long, and 4 parts reach 1.
Each part is $\frac{1}{3}$ long, and 3 parts reach 1.
questions.answer: Each part is $\frac{1}{3}$ long, and 3 parts reach 1.
questions.solution: 3 equal parts make the whole length 1, so each part is 1/3 long and 3 of them reach 1.

solve.answer: Each part is $\frac{1}{3}$ long, and 3 parts reach 1.

questions.skill: Make a fraction on a number line by equal jumps from 0
questions.stem: Rob starts at 0 on a number line cut into eighths. He jumps $\frac{1}{8}$ forward five times, then jumps back 2 parts. What fraction is he at now?
questions.solution: Five jumps forward land at 5/8. Two parts back is 5/8 - 2/8 = 3/8.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions on an area or length model
questions.stem: A bar is cut into 2 equal parts and 1 part is shaded. A bar of the same size is cut into 4 equal parts. How many of the 4 parts must be shaded to cover the same amount?
questions.solution: Cutting each half into 2 equal parts makes 4 parts in all. The 1 shaded half becomes 2 shaded parts, so 2 of the 4 parts must be shaded.

solve.work: 1/2 = 2/4: each half is 2 fourths, so 2 of the 4 parts.

questions.skill: Identify equivalent fractions
questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to $\frac{1}{2}$?
questions.solution: Cut each half into 2 equal parts. Then 1 half is the same as 2 of 4 equal parts, so $\frac{1}{2}$ = $\frac{2}{4}$.

solve.work: 1/2 = 2/4 (each half split in two). 1/4, 2/3, 1/3 are not half.

questions.skill: Fractions equal to one
questions.stem: Mia ate $\frac{8}{8}$ of a pizza. How many whole pizzas did she eat?
questions.solution: A pizza cut into 8 equal slices has 8 slices in all. Eating all 8 slices is the same as eating 1 whole pizza.

questions.skill: Fractions equal to one
questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to 1?
questions.solution: A fraction is equal to 1 when the numerator and the denominator are the same, because all of the equal parts are counted. So $\frac{4}{4}$ = 1.

questions.skill: Fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: Sam has 6 pieces of sandwich. Each piece is $\frac{1}{3}$ of a whole sandwich. How many whole sandwiches does Sam have?
questions.solution: Every 3 pieces make 1 whole sandwich. 6 pieces make 2 whole sandwiches.

solve.work: 6 pieces of 1/3 = 6/3; 3 thirds make 1, so 6 thirds make 2.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions on a number line
questions.stem: On a number line, the space from 0 to 1 is split into 2 equal parts, so $\frac{1}{2}$ is halfway. Now the space from 0 to 1 is split into 4 equal parts instead. Which fraction names the halfway point?
questions.solution: With 4 equal parts, the halfway point is 2 parts from 0. That point is $\frac{2}{4}$, the same point as $\frac{1}{2}$.

solve.work: Halfway between 0 and 1 with 4 parts is the 2nd mark: 2/4.

questions.skill: Find a missing number in equivalent fractions
questions.stem: A strip is cut into 3 equal parts, and 1 part is colored. The same strip is cut into 6 equal parts. Fill in the ?: $\frac{1}{3}$ = $\frac{?}{6}$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Cutting each third in half makes 6 equal parts. The 1 colored third is now 2 of the 6 parts, so the ? is 2.

solve.work: Each third splits into 2 sixths, so 1/3 = 2/6.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions on an area or length model
questions.stem: Two bars are the same size. The first bar is cut into 3 equal parts and 1 part is shaded. The second bar is cut into 6 equal parts. How many parts of the second bar must be shaded to match the first?
questions.solution: Each third of the first bar is 2 of the 6 equal parts of the second bar. So 2 parts must be shaded.

questions.skill: Find a missing number in equivalent fractions
questions.stem: Fill in the ?: $\frac{2}{4}$ = $\frac{1}{?}$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Two of 4 equal parts is the same amount as 1 of 2 equal parts, because 2 fourths is 1 half. So the ? is 2.

questions.skill: Fractions equal to one
questions.stem: A fraction has the same numerator and denominator, like $\frac{5}{5}$. What is it equal to?
questions.solution: When the numerator and denominator are the same, every equal part is counted. That is 1 whole, so $\frac{5}{5}$ = 1.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions on an area or length model
questions.stem: A ribbon is cut into 4 equal parts and 3 parts are colored red. A ribbon of the same length is cut into 8 equal parts. How many of the 8 parts must be colored red to match?
questions.solution: Each fourth is 2 eighths. So 3 fourths is 3 x 2 = 6 eighths, and 6 of the 8 parts must be colored.

questions.skill: Identify equivalent fractions
questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to $\frac{3}{4}$?
questions.solution: Cut each fourth into 2 equal parts. Then 3 fourths becomes 6 eighths, so $\frac{3}{4}$ = $\frac{6}{8}$.

questions.skill: Find a missing number in equivalent fractions
questions.stem: Fill in the ?: $\frac{4}{6}$ = $\frac{2}{?}$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Group the 6 equal parts in twos to make 3 equal parts. The 4 sixths become 2 thirds, so the ? is 3.

questions.skill: Fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to 3?
questions.solution: Each whole has 2 halves, so 3 wholes have 3 x 2 = 6 halves. So $\frac{6}{2}$ = 3.

solve.work: 6/2 = 3 (2 halves per whole, 6 halves = 3 wholes). 6/3 = 2, others < 1.

questions.skill: Fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: A ribbon is $\frac{12}{4}$ meters long. How many whole meters long is it?
questions.solution: Every 4 fourths make 1 whole meter. 12 fourths make 12 / 4 = 3 whole meters.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions on a number line
questions.stem: A number line from 0 to 1 is split into 8 equal parts. A point is at $\frac{4}{8}$. If the number line is split into halves instead, which fraction names the same point?
questions.solution: 4 of 8 equal parts is half of the way from 0 to 1. So $\frac{4}{8}$ = $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Find a missing number in equivalent fractions
questions.stem: A path is cut into 6 equal sections. Jo has walked 3 sections, which is $\frac{3}{6}$ of the path. This is the same as $\frac{?}{2}$ of the path. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Pair up the 6 sections to make 2 equal halves. 3 sections make 1 of those halves, so the ? is 1.

questions.skill: Explain why fractions are equivalent
questions.stem: Lena says $\frac{2}{3}$ and $\frac{4}{6}$ are equal. Which statement shows why she is right?
choices: Each fraction is exactly 1 part away from a whole
Adding 2 to the top and the bottom of the first fraction gives the second
Both fractions have the same denominator
Cutting each third into 2 equal parts makes 6 parts, and 2 thirds become 4 sixths
questions.answer: Cutting each third into 2 equal parts makes 6 parts, and 2 thirds become 4 sixths
questions.solution: Cut each third into 2 equal parts. The 3 thirds become 6 sixths, and the 2 colored thirds become 4 sixths. So $\frac{2}{3}$ = $\frac{4}{6}$.

solve.answer: Cutting each third into 2 equal parts makes 6 parts, and 2 thirds become 4 sixths
solve.work: Splitting each third into 2 gives sixths; 2 thirds become 4 sixths. Other statements are false or irrelevant (different denominators; adding 2 is invalid reasoning; distance from whole differs: 1/3 vs 2/6 would be equal but "1 part" is not true for both).

questions.skill: Fractions equal to one
questions.stem: A fraction is equal to 1 and its denominator is 6. What is its numerator?
questions.solution: A fraction equals 1 when its numerator and denominator are the same. With a denominator of 6, the numerator is also 6: $\frac{6}{6}$ = 1.

questions.skill: Identify equivalent fractions
questions.stem: Which pair of fractions is equal?
questions.solution: Cutting each third in half gives 2 thirds = 4 sixths. In the other pairs, the fractions name different amounts: for example, 1 third is more than 1 sixth.

solve.work: 2/3 = 4/6. 2/3 vs 3/4 differ, 1/3 vs 1/6 differ, 2/4 vs 2/8 differ.

questions.skill: Find a missing number in equivalent fractions
questions.stem: Fill in the ?: $\frac{6}{8}$ = $\frac{3}{?}$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Group the 8 equal parts in twos to make 4 equal parts. The 6 eighths become 3 fourths, so the ? is 4.

questions.skill: Identify equivalent fractions
questions.stem: Which list shows only fractions that are equal to $\frac{1}{2}$?
questions.solution: Half of 4 is 2, half of 6 is 3 and half of 8 is 4. So $\frac{2}{4}$, $\frac{3}{6}$ and $\frac{4}{8}$ are all equal to $\frac{1}{2}$. The other lists each have a fraction that is not: $\frac{2}{6}$, $\frac{1}{4}$ or $\frac{5}{8}$.

questions.skill: Fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: A fraction is equal to 4 and its denominator is 3. What is its numerator?
questions.solution: Each whole is 3 thirds, so 4 wholes are 4 x 3 = 12 thirds. The numerator is 12.

questions.skill: Fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT equal to a whole number?
questions.solution: Divide the numerator by the denominator. 6 / 3 = 2, 6 / 2 = 3 and 6 / 6 = 1 are whole numbers. 6 / 4 is between 1 and 2, so $\frac{6}{4}$ is not a whole number.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions on an area or length model
questions.stem: Three bars are the same size. The first is cut into 4 equal parts with 2 parts shaded. The second is cut into 8 equal parts with 4 parts shaded. The third is cut into 6 equal parts. How many of its 6 parts must be shaded to match the first two?
questions.solution: 2 of 4 parts is half the bar, and so is 4 of 8 parts. Half of the third bar is 6 / 2 = 3 of its 6 parts.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions on a number line
questions.stem: A number line goes from 0 to 2, and each whole is split into thirds. A point is at $\frac{6}{3}$. Which whole number names the same point?
questions.solution: Each whole has 3 thirds, so 6 thirds make 6 / 3 = 2 wholes. The point is at 2.

solve.work: 6 thirds = 2 wholes, so the point is at 2.

questions.skill: Fractions equal to one
questions.stem: Nina colors $\frac{4}{4}$ of one bar and $\frac{6}{6}$ of another bar. The bars are the same size. How many whole bars did she color in all?
questions.solution: Coloring 4 of 4 equal parts is 1 whole bar, and coloring 6 of 6 equal parts is 1 whole bar. 1 + 1 = 2 whole bars.

questions.skill: Explain why fractions are equivalent
questions.stem: Ravi says $\frac{3}{4}$ = $\frac{3}{8}$ because both fractions have 3 on top. Which statement shows his mistake?
choices: 3 of 8 equal parts covers more of a bar than 3 of 4 equal parts
Both fractions are equal to 1 whole, so they are not equal to each other
3 of 8 equal parts covers less of a bar than 3 of 4 equal parts
A fraction can only be equal to one with the same denominator
questions.answer: 3 of 8 equal parts covers less of a bar than 3 of 4 equal parts
questions.solution: Eighths are smaller parts than fourths. So 3 eighths covers less of the bar than 3 fourths, and the fractions are not equal. Equal fractions need the same amount of the whole, not the same numerator.

solve.answer: 3 of 8 equal parts covers less of a bar than 3 of 4 equal parts
solve.work: Eighths are smaller than fourths, so 3/8 covers less than 3/4. Other options are false.

questions.skill: Equivalent fractions on an area or length model
questions.stem: Mia and Leo each have a sandwich of the same size. Mia cuts hers into 3 equal parts and eats 2 of them. Leo cuts his into 6 equal parts. How many parts must Leo eat to have eaten the same amount as Mia?
questions.solution: Each third is 2 sixths. Mia ate 2 thirds, which is 2 x 2 = 4 sixths, so Leo must eat 4 parts.

questions.skill: Fractions equal to whole numbers
questions.stem: A teacher cuts each sheet of paper into 2 equal halves and makes 18 halves in all. How many whole sheets of paper did she use?
questions.solution: Every 2 halves make 1 whole sheet. 18 halves make 18 / 2 = 9 whole sheets.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: Which fraction is greater, $\frac{2}{8}$ or $\frac{5}{8}$? Write the greater fraction.
questions.solution: Both fractions are eighths, so the pieces are the same size. 5 pieces are more than 2 pieces, so $\frac{5}{8}$ is greater.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: Which comparison of fractions is correct?
questions.solution: When the denominators are the same, the fraction with the greater numerator is greater. 2 sixths is less than 4 sixths, so $\frac{2}{6} < \frac{4}{6}$ is true. In the other statements the symbol points the wrong way or the fractions are not equal.

solve.work: 1/3<2/3 so A false; 2/6<4/6 true; 3/4>1/4 so C false; 5/8>3/8 so D false.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: Which fraction is less than $\frac{4}{8}$?
questions.solution: All of the fractions are eighths, so compare the numerators. 3 is less than 4, so $\frac{3}{8}$ is less than $\frac{4}{8}$. 5 and 7 are greater than 4, and $\frac{4}{8}$ is equal to itself.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Compare $\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{6}$. Which fraction is greater? Write that fraction.
questions.solution: Both fractions have 1 part. Thirds are bigger pieces than sixths, because the whole is cut into fewer parts. So $\frac{1}{3}$ is greater than $\frac{1}{6}$.

solve.work: Same numerator; thirds are bigger than sixths, so 1/3 > 1/6.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Zoe compares fractions that have the same numerator. Which of her sentences is true?
questions.solution: Both fractions have 3 parts. Fourths are bigger than sixths, so 3 fourths is more than 3 sixths: $\frac{3}{4} > \frac{3}{6}$. In the other statements, the symbol points the wrong way or the fractions are not equal.

solve.work: Same numerator 3; fourths are bigger than sixths so 3/4 > 3/6; sixths bigger than eighths so 3/8 < 3/6.

questions.skill: Compare fractions in a story about the same whole
questions.stem: Ava ran $\frac{3}{8}$ of a mile. Ben ran $\frac{5}{8}$ of a mile. Who ran farther?
questions.solution: Both distances are in eighths of a mile. 5 eighths is more than 3 eighths, so Ben ran farther.

questions.skill: Compare fractions in a story about the same whole
questions.stem: Noah drank $\frac{1}{2}$ of a glass of juice. Emma drank $\frac{1}{4}$ of an identical glass of juice. Write the fraction for the person who drank more.
questions.solution: Both glasses are the same size, so we can compare. Each person drank 1 part, and halves are bigger than fourths. Noah drank more, which is $\frac{1}{2}$ of a glass.

solve.work: Identical glasses; halves bigger than fourths: 1/2 > 1/4. Noah drank more.

questions.skill: Choose the symbols >, < and = that make a comparison true
questions.stem: Which two symbols make both sentences true? $\frac{1}{4}$ ? $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$ ? $\frac{1}{8}$
questions.solution: In the first sentence the denominators are the same, and 1 is less than 3, so $\frac{1}{4} < \frac{3}{4}$. In the second the numerators are the same, and fourths are bigger than eighths, so $\frac{1}{4} > \frac{1}{8}$.

questions.skill: Know the wholes must be the same size
questions.stem: When we compare two fractions, what must be true about their wholes?
choices: The wholes must be the same size.
The wholes must be different sizes.
The wholes must both be circles.
The wholes must both be cut into 4 parts.
questions.answer: The wholes must be the same size.
questions.solution: Half of a big pizza and half of a tiny pizza are not the same amount. To compare fractions fairly, both must be fractions of the same whole, or wholes that are the same size.

solve.answer: The wholes must be the same size.
solve.work: Fractions compare only when they are of the same whole (same size).

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Four wholes are the same size. Each fraction below is the size of one equal part of a different whole. Which fraction shows the biggest part?
questions.solution: All four fractions have 1 part. The fewer parts a whole is cut into, the bigger each part is. The whole cut into 3 parts has the biggest parts.

solve.work: Same-size wholes, unit fractions: fewer parts means bigger parts. 3 is the fewest, so 1/3 is biggest.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: How many of these fractions are less than $\frac{3}{4}$: $\frac{1}{4}$, $\frac{2}{4}$, $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{4}{4}$?
questions.solution: All of the fractions are fourths, so compare the numerators with 3. 1 and 2 are less than 3. 3 is equal to 3 and 4 is greater than 3. So 2 of the fractions are less than $\frac{3}{4}$.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: Which statement is NOT true?
questions.solution: All of the fractions are sixths, so compare the numerators. 4 is less than 5, so $\frac{4}{6}$ is less than $\frac{5}{6}$, and the statement $\frac{4}{6} > \frac{5}{6}$ is not true. The other three statements are true.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Compare $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\frac{3}{8}$. Write the lesser fraction.
questions.solution: Both fractions have 3 parts. Eighths are smaller pieces than fourths, so 3 eighths is less than 3 fourths. The lesser fraction is $\frac{3}{8}$.

solve.work: Same numerator; eighths smaller than fourths, so 3/8 is lesser.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Which fraction is the least?
questions.solution: Every fraction has a numerator of 2, so compare the sizes of the pieces. Eighths are the smallest pieces, so 2 eighths is the least.

solve.work: Same numerator 2; the largest denominator gives the smallest: 2/8.

questions.skill: Order three or more fractions
questions.stem: Mia puts three number cards in a row, with the least fraction on the left and the greatest on the right. The cards are $\frac{5}{6}$, $\frac{2}{6}$ and $\frac{3}{6}$. Which row is right?
questions.solution: All are sixths, so put the numerators in order: 2, 3, 5. The list is $\frac{2}{6}$, $\frac{3}{6}$, $\frac{5}{6}$.

questions.skill: Order three or more fractions
questions.stem: Which list shows the fractions in order from greatest to least?
questions.solution: Every fraction has 3 parts, so the bigger the pieces, the greater the fraction. Fourths are the biggest, then sixths, then eighths. The order from greatest to least is $\frac{3}{4}$, $\frac{3}{6}$, $\frac{3}{8}$.

questions.skill: Find a missing numerator or denominator that makes a comparison true
questions.stem: What is the greatest whole number that can go in the ? so that $\frac{?}{6} < \frac{4}{6}$ is true?
questions.solution: Both fractions are sixths, so the numerator in the ? must be less than 4. The greatest whole number less than 4 is 3.

questions.skill: Compare fractions in a story about the same whole
questions.stem: Pia filled $\frac{1}{3}$ of a jar with sand. Quinn filled $\frac{1}{4}$ of an identical jar with sand. Whose jar has more sand?
choices: Both jars have the same amount of sand.
questions.solution: The jars are identical, so we can compare. Each person filled 1 part, and thirds are bigger than fourths. So Pia's jar has more sand.

solve.work: Identical jars; thirds bigger than fourths: 1/3 > 1/4. Pia.

questions.skill: Compare fractions in a story about the same whole
questions.stem: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Tara ate $\frac{2}{8}$ of the pizza. Vic ate $\frac{4}{8}$ of the same pizza. Uma ate more pizza than Tara but less than Vic. She ate a whole number of slices. How many slices did Uma eat?
questions.solution: Tara ate 2 slices and Vic ate 4 slices. Uma ate more than 2 slices and less than 4 slices, so she ate 3 slices.

solve.work: Tara 2 slices, Vic 4; more than 2 and less than 4 is 3 slices.

questions.skill: Choose the symbols >, < and = that make a comparison true
questions.stem: Which two symbols make both sentences true? $\frac{3}{6}$ ? $\frac{3}{6}$ and $\frac{3}{6}$ ? $\frac{3}{3}$
questions.solution: The fractions in the first sentence are exactly the same, so they are equal. In the second, the numerators are the same, and sixths are smaller pieces than thirds, so $\frac{3}{6} < \frac{3}{3}$.

solve.work: 3/6 = 3/6; same numerator, thirds bigger than sixths so 3/6 < 3/3. "= and <".

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same denominator
questions.stem: Rosa compares $\frac{5}{6}$ and $\frac{3}{6}$ and says $\frac{5}{6}$ is greater. Which sentence gives the correct reason?
choices: The 5 is greater than the 6, so the pieces are bigger.
Both are sixths, and 5 sixths is more pieces than 3 sixths.
The numerators are different, so the pieces are different sizes.
Both have 6 on the bottom, so the fractions are equal.
questions.answer: Both are sixths, and 5 sixths is more pieces than 3 sixths.
questions.solution: Both fractions are sixths, so the pieces are the same size. 5 pieces are more than 3 pieces, so $\frac{5}{6}$ is greater than $\frac{3}{6}$.

solve.answer: Both are sixths, and 5 sixths is more pieces than 3 sixths.
solve.work: Same-size pieces (sixths); 5 of them is more than 3.

questions.skill: Compare fractions with the same numerator
questions.stem: Max says, "Since 8 is greater than 6, $\frac{4}{8}$ is greater than $\frac{4}{6}$." Which sentence compares the fractions correctly?
choices: Eighths are bigger pieces than sixths, so $\frac{4}{8}$ is greater than $\frac{4}{6}$.
The numerators are the same, so the two fractions are equal.
Eighths are smaller pieces than sixths, so $\frac{4}{8}$ is less than $\frac{4}{6}$.
The denominators are different, so they cannot be compared.
questions.answer: Eighths are smaller pieces than sixths, so $\frac{4}{8}$ is less than $\frac{4}{6}$.
questions.solution: Both fractions have 4 parts. The more parts a whole is cut into, the smaller each part is. Eighths are smaller than sixths, so 4 eighths is less than 4 sixths.

solve.answer: Eighths are smaller pieces than sixths, so $\frac{4}{8}$ is less than $\frac{4}{6}$.
solve.work: Same numerator 4; eighths are smaller than sixths, so 4/8 < 4/6.

questions.skill: Order three or more fractions
questions.stem: Put $\frac{3}{8}$, $\frac{1}{8}$, $\frac{6}{8}$ and $\frac{4}{8}$ in order from least to greatest. Which fraction is third?
questions.solution: All are eighths, so order the numerators: 1, 3, 4, 6. The order is $\frac{1}{8}$, $\frac{3}{8}$, $\frac{4}{8}$, $\frac{6}{8}$. The third fraction is $\frac{4}{8}$.

questions.skill: Order three or more fractions
questions.stem: Put $\frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{2}{8}$, $\frac{2}{4}$ and $\frac{2}{6}$ in order from greatest to least. Which fraction is second?
questions.solution: Every fraction has 2 parts, so the bigger the pieces, the greater the fraction. From biggest pieces to smallest: thirds, fourths, sixths, eighths. The order is $\frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{2}{4}$, $\frac{2}{6}$, $\frac{2}{8}$. The second fraction is $\frac{2}{4}$.

solve.work: Same numerator, greatest to least: 2/3, 2/4, 2/6, 2/8. Second is 2/4.

questions.skill: Find a missing numerator or denominator that makes a comparison true
questions.stem: The ? in $\frac{1}{?}$ can be 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8. For how many of these numbers is $\frac{1}{?}$ greater than $\frac{1}{6}$?
questions.solution: Each fraction has 1 part, so a fraction is greater than $\frac{1}{6}$ when its pieces are bigger than sixths. That happens when the denominator is less than 6: 2, 3 and 4. That is 3 numbers. A denominator of 6 gives an equal fraction, and 8 gives a lesser one.

questions.skill: Find a missing numerator or denominator that makes a comparison true
questions.stem: A whole number n makes $\frac{n}{8}$ greater than $\frac{3}{8}$ and less than $\frac{7}{8}$. How many different whole numbers n work?
questions.solution: All are eighths, so n must be greater than 3 and less than 7. The numbers are 4, 5 and 6. That is 3 numbers.

questions.skill: Find a missing numerator or denominator that makes a comparison true
questions.stem: Which fraction could go in the ? to make this true? $\frac{1}{4} < ? < \frac{3}{4}$
questions.solution: All are fourths, so the numerator in the ? must be greater than 1 and less than 3. The only choice is 2, so the fraction is $\frac{2}{4}$.

questions.skill: Find a missing numerator or denominator that makes a comparison true
questions.stem: The ? in $\frac{2}{?}$ is one of 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8. Which number for the ? makes $\frac{2}{8} < \frac{2}{?} < \frac{2}{4}$ true?
questions.solution: All the fractions have 2 parts, so the fraction in the middle must have pieces smaller than fourths and bigger than eighths. Of the choices, only sixths fit between them. So the ? is 6.

questions.skill: Compare fractions in a story about the same whole
questions.stem: Three friends have granola bars that are all the same size. Ira ate $\frac{2}{8}$ of his bar, Joy ate $\frac{2}{3}$ of hers and Ken ate $\frac{2}{4}$ of his. Write the fraction for the friend who ate the most.
questions.solution: Each friend ate 2 parts, so compare the sizes of the pieces. Thirds are bigger than fourths, and fourths are bigger than eighths. Joy ate the most, which is $\frac{2}{3}$ of a bar.

solve.work: Same-size bars, same numerator 2: thirds are biggest, so 2/3 (Joy) is most.

questions.skill: Know the wholes must be the same size
questions.stem: Hana ate $\frac{1}{2}$ of a small pizza. Ian ate $\frac{1}{4}$ of a very large pizza. Hana says she ate more than Ian because $\frac{1}{2}$ is greater than $\frac{1}{4}$. Why might she be wrong?
choices: Fractions with a 1 on top are always equal to each other.
Fourths are bigger than halves, so Ian must have eaten more.
The pizzas are not the same size, so the fractions are of different wholes.
Fractions with different denominators can never be compared.
questions.answer: The pizzas are not the same size, so the fractions are of different wholes.
questions.solution: We can say $\frac{1}{2}$ is greater than $\frac{1}{4}$ only when both are parts of the same whole. A half of a small pizza can be less than a quarter of a very large pizza.

solve.answer: The pizzas are not the same size, so the fractions are of different wholes.
solve.work: Different-size pizzas, so the fractions are of different wholes and cannot be compared that way.

questions.skill: Read the time from the clock hands
questions.stem: On a clock, the hour hand is just past the 3. The minute hand points at the 4. Each number on the clock stands for 5 minutes: the 1 is 5 minutes, the 2 is 10, and so on. How many minutes after 3 o'clock is it?
questions.solution: The 4 stands for 4 x 5 = 20 minutes. It is 20 minutes after 3 o'clock, or 3:20.

solve.work: Minute hand at 4 -> 4 x 5 = 20 minutes after 3.

questions.skill: Write a time in different ways
questions.stem: A digital clock shows 7:09. Which tells the same time?
questions.solution: 7:09 means 9 minutes past the hour of 7. So it is 9 minutes after 7.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: A game starts at 3:10 and ends at 3:35. How many minutes does the game last?
questions.solution: Both times are in the 3 o'clock hour. 35 - 10 = 25 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: Art class starts at 9:20 and lasts 15 minutes. What time does it end?
questions.solution: 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 35 minutes past 9. The class ends at 9:35.

questions.skill: Write a time in different ways
questions.stem: A digital clock shows 5:40. Which tells the same time?
questions.solution: From 5:40 to 6:00 is 20 minutes. So 5:40 is 20 minutes to 6.

questions.skill: Read the time from the clock hands
questions.stem: The hour hand is between the 8 and the 9. The minute hand points straight down at the 6. Each number on the clock stands for 5 minutes: the 1 is 5 minutes, the 2 is 10, and so on. What time is it?
questions.solution: The hour hand is past the 8 but not yet at the 9, so the hour is 8. The 6 stands for 30 minutes. The time is 8:30.

solve.work: Hour hand between 8 and 9 -> 8; minute hand at 6 -> 30 minutes. 8:30.

questions.skill: Use a.m. and p.m.
questions.stem: School starts at 8:30 in the morning. Which shows that time correctly?
questions.solution: Times from midnight to noon are a.m. Morning is a.m., so school starts at 8:30 a.m.

solve.issues: a.m./p.m. is mainly a Grade 2 skill (NC.2.MD.7); only loosely tests telling time to the minute.
solve.work: School in the morning -> a.m.; 8:30 written 8:30 a.m.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: Dee gets on a bus at 2:50. She gets off at 3:10. How many minutes is she on the bus?
questions.solution: From 2:50 to 3:00 is 10 minutes. From 3:00 to 3:10 is 10 more minutes. 10 + 10 = 20 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A play ended at 6:40 after lasting 25 minutes. What time did it start?
questions.solution: Go back 25 minutes from 6:40. 40 - 25 = 15, so it started at 6:15.

questions.skill: Read the time from the clock hands
questions.stem: A digital clock shows 4:07. How many minutes after 4 o'clock is it?
questions.solution: The number after the colon tells the minutes. It is 7 minutes after 4 o'clock.

questions.skill: Read the time from the clock hands
questions.stem: On a clock, the minute hand is 2 small marks past the 5. Each number on the clock stands for 5 minutes: the 1 is 5 minutes, the 2 is 10, and so on. How many minutes after the hour is it?
questions.solution: The 5 stands for 25 minutes. Two more small marks make 25 + 2 = 27 minutes after the hour.

solve.work: The 5 is 25 minutes; 2 small marks more = 27.

questions.skill: Read the time from the clock hands
questions.stem: The hour hand is between the 10 and the 11, closer to the 11. The minute hand points at the 9. Each number on the clock stands for 5 minutes: the 1 is 5 minutes, the 2 is 10, and so on. What time is it?
questions.solution: The hour hand has not reached the 11, so the hour is 10. The 9 stands for 9 x 5 = 45 minutes. The time is 10:45.

solve.work: Hour hand between 10 and 11 -> hour is 10; minute hand at 9 -> 45 minutes. 10:45 (hand closer to 11 is consistent with 45 min).

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: Choir practice starts at 7:42 and ends at 8:05. How many minutes does practice last?
questions.solution: From 7:42 to 8:00 is 18 minutes. From 8:00 to 8:05 is 5 more minutes. 18 + 5 = 23 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A movie starts at 11:40 and lasts 35 minutes. What time does it end?
questions.solution: From 11:40 to 12:00 is 20 minutes. There are 35 - 20 = 15 minutes left to add. The movie ends at 12:15.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: Tia's swim lesson lasted 40 minutes and ended at 5:15. What time did it start?
questions.solution: From 5:15 back to 5:00 is 15 minutes. There are 40 - 15 = 25 minutes more to go back from 5:00, which is 4:35.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: The clock shows 6:48. How many minutes are there until 7:00?
questions.solution: From 6:48 to 7:00 is 60 - 48 = 12 minutes.

questions.skill: Write a time in different ways
questions.stem: Which time is 14 minutes before 3:00?
questions.solution: Going back 14 minutes from 3:00 gets to 2:46, because 60 - 14 = 46 minutes past 2.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: Rosa starts her homework at 4:18 and finishes at 4:57. How many minutes does she work?
questions.solution: Both times are in the 4 o'clock hour. 57 - 18 = 39 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: Sam eats lunch at 12:20. His soccer game starts 40 minutes later. What time does the game start?
questions.solution: From 12:20 to 1:00 is 40 minutes. The game starts at 1:00.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: At 2:30 Ken sets a timer for 45 minutes. At 2:50, how many minutes are left on the timer?
questions.solution: From 2:30 to 2:50 is 20 minutes gone. 45 - 20 = 25 minutes are left.

solve.work: Timer ends at 2:30 + 45 = 3:15. From 2:50 to 3:15 = 25 minutes. (Or 45 - 20 elapsed = 25.)

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: A train leaves at 10:47 and arrives at 11:29. How many minutes is the trip?
questions.solution: From 10:47 to 11:00 is 13 minutes. From 11:00 to 11:29 is 29 more minutes. 13 + 29 = 42 minutes.

questions.skill: Find the end time
questions.stem: A concert starts at 7:48 and lasts 38 minutes. What time does it end?
questions.solution: From 7:48 to 8:00 is 12 minutes. There are 38 - 12 = 26 minutes left to add. The concert ends at 8:26.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: Tim starts to practice piano at 3:10. He plays for 15 minutes, rests for 5 minutes, then plays for 20 minutes. How many minutes after 3:00 does he finish?
questions.solution: He is done after 15 + 5 + 20 = 40 minutes, which is at 3:50. That is 50 minutes after 3:00.

questions.skill: Find the start time
questions.stem: A bike ride lasted 52 minutes and ended at 9:14. What time did it start?
questions.solution: From 9:14 back to 9:00 is 14 minutes. There are 52 - 14 = 38 more minutes to go back from 9:00. 60 - 38 = 22, so the ride started at 8:22.

questions.skill: Read the time from the clock hands
questions.stem: On a clock, the minute hand is 3 small marks before the 10. Each number on the clock stands for 5 minutes: the 1 is 5 minutes, the 2 is 10, and so on. How many minutes after the hour is it?
questions.solution: The 10 stands for 50 minutes. Three small marks before it is 50 - 3 = 47 minutes after the hour.

solve.work: The 10 is 50 minutes; 3 small marks before = 47.

questions.skill: Write a time in different ways
questions.stem: A digital clock shows 3:56. Which tells the same time?
questions.solution: From 3:56 to 4:00 is 4 minutes. So 3:56 is 4 minutes to 4.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: A cake needs 35 minutes in the oven. Dana puts it in at 4:40. She takes it out at 5:20. How many minutes too long is it in the oven?
questions.solution: From 4:40 to 5:20 is 20 + 20 = 40 minutes. The cake needs 35 minutes. 40 - 35 = 5 minutes too long.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: Which activity takes the most time?
questions.solution: Reading takes 28 minutes. Music takes 25 minutes. Art takes 30 minutes. Games take 20 + 5 = 25 minutes. Art takes the most time.

solve.work: Reading 28 min; Art 30 min; Music 25 min; Games 25 min. Art is longest.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: The pool closes at 2:00 p.m. A clock shows 1:37 p.m. How many minutes until the pool closes?
questions.solution: From 1:37 to 2:00 is 60 - 37 = 23 minutes.

questions.skill: Find elapsed time within one hour
questions.stem: Which pair of times is exactly 45 minutes apart?
questions.solution: From 2:10 to 2:55 is 55 - 10 = 45 minutes. The others are 55, 25 and 35 minutes apart.

questions.skill: Choose the best customary unit
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring how much juice fits in a small glass?
questions.solution: Juice in a glass is a liquid, so we measure its capacity. A glass holds about a cup. A gallon is far too big, and pounds and yards do not measure capacity.

solve.work: A small glass holds about 1 cup. Gallons too big; pounds and feet do not measure capacity.

questions.skill: Choose the best customary unit
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the weight of a watermelon?
questions.solution: A watermelon is heavy, about 10 pounds. Ounces are for light things, inches measure length, and gallons measure capacity. Pounds is best.

solve.work: A watermelon weighs about 10-20 pounds. Ounces too small; inches and gallons are not weight.

questions.skill: Choose the best customary unit
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the length of a postage stamp?
questions.solution: A stamp is tiny, and length is measured in inches, feet or yards. Of these, an inch is the smallest, so inches fit best. Pounds measure weight.

solve.work: A stamp is about 1 inch long. Inches.

questions.skill: Measure a length with a ruler
questions.stem: A ribbon lies along a ruler. One end is at the 0-inch mark and the other end is at the 8-inch mark. How many inches long is the ribbon?
questions.solution: The ribbon starts at 0, so the mark where it ends tells its length. It is 8 inches long.

questions.skill: Choose a reasonable estimate of a length, capacity or weight
questions.stem: Which is the most reasonable weight for a loaf of bread?
questions.solution: A loaf of bread is about as heavy as a small bag of sugar, around 1 pound. 1 ounce is as light as a few coins, and 10 or 100 pounds is far too heavy.

solve.work: A loaf of bread weighs about 1 pound (16-24 oz). 1 oz too light, 10 and 100 lb too heavy.

questions.skill: Choose a reasonable estimate of a length, capacity or weight
questions.stem: Which is the most reasonable amount of water in a full kitchen sink?
questions.solution: A full sink holds a good amount of water, around 10 gallons. 1 cup and 10 cups would barely cover the bottom, and 100 gallons would fill a bathtub twice over.

solve.work: A full kitchen sink holds several gallons, about 10. 1 or 10 cups (under a gallon) is too little, 100 gallons too much.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step length problem
questions.stem: A rope is 9 feet long. Jan cuts off 4 feet. How many feet long is the rope now?
questions.solution: Cutting off 4 feet takes away from the rope: 9 - 4 = 5. The rope is 5 feet long.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step capacity problem
questions.stem: Tom pours 3 cups of juice into a pitcher and then 4 more cups. How many cups of juice are in the pitcher?
questions.solution: Put the amounts together: 3 + 4 = 7 cups.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step weight problem
questions.stem: A bag of apples weighs 5 pounds. A bag of oranges weighs 4 pounds. How many pounds do the two bags weigh together?
questions.solution: Add the weights: 5 + 4 = 9 pounds.

questions.skill: Choose a reasonable estimate of a length, capacity or weight
questions.stem: A car is parked in a driveway. Which is the most reasonable length for the car?
questions.solution: A car is longer than a bed but shorter than a bus, about 15 feet. 15 inches and 1 foot are about as long as a shoe, and 15 yards is longer than a bus.

solve.work: A car is about 15 feet long. 1 ft and 15 in too short, 15 yd (45 ft) too long.

questions.skill: Choose the best customary unit
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring how much gasoline fits in a car's tank?
questions.solution: A gas tank holds a lot of liquid, about 15 gallons. A cup and a teaspoon are much too small, and inches measure length, not capacity.

solve.work: A car tank holds about 12-15 gallons. Gallons.

questions.skill: Choose the best customary unit
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the weight of a pencil?
questions.solution: A pencil is very light. Ounces measure small weights; a pound is much heavier than a pencil. Gallons measure capacity and feet measure length.

solve.work: A pencil weighs well under an ounce; ounces is the best weight unit offered.

questions.skill: Measure a length with a ruler
questions.stem: A paper strip is placed along a ruler. Its left end is at the 2-inch mark and its right end is at the 11-inch mark. How many inches long is the strip?
questions.solution: The strip does not start at 0. Its length is the difference between the two marks: 11 - 2 = 9 inches.

questions.skill: Choose a reasonable estimate of a length, capacity or weight
questions.stem: Which is the most reasonable weight for a house cat?
questions.solution: A house cat weighs about 10 pounds. 10 ounces and 1 ounce are too light for a cat, and 100 pounds is as heavy as a grown-up.

solve.work: A house cat weighs about 10 pounds.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step length problem
questions.stem: A track is 36 yards long. A runner has already run 14 yards of it. How many more yards does the runner have to go?
questions.solution: Take what is already run from the whole track: 36 - 14 = 22. The runner has 22 yards to go.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step length problem
questions.stem: A ribbon is 20 inches long. Sam cuts it into 4 pieces of the same length. How long is each piece?
questions.solution: Share 20 inches equally among 4 pieces: 20 / 4 = 5. Each piece is 5 inches long.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step capacity problem
questions.stem: A bucket holds 12 quarts of water. Dina uses 5 quarts to water some plants. How many quarts are left in the bucket?
questions.solution: Subtract what was used: 12 - 5 = 7 quarts.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step capacity problem
questions.stem: A pitcher holds 8 cups of water. Each glass holds 2 cups. How many glasses can be filled from a full pitcher?
questions.solution: Divide the 8 cups into glasses of 2 cups: 8 / 2 = 4. Four glasses can be filled.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step weight problem
questions.stem: Each box of crackers weighs 8 ounces. Ben buys 6 boxes. How many ounces do the boxes weigh in all?
questions.solution: 6 boxes of 8 ounces each: 8 x 6 = 48 ounces.

questions.skill: Choose a reasonable estimate of a length, capacity or weight
questions.stem: Which is the most reasonable amount of water in a full bathtub?
questions.solution: A bathtub holds a lot of water, about 40 gallons. 40 cups is only about 2 gallons, 4 pints is half a gallon, and 400 gallons is far more than a tub can hold.

solve.work: A full bathtub holds about 40-50 gallons. 40 cups is 2.5 gallons, 4 pints half a gallon, 400 gallons far too much.

questions.skill: Measure a length with a ruler
questions.stem: Mia lines up a book with the 0-inch mark of a ruler, and its other edge is at the 9-inch mark. Dev lines up the same book with its left edge at the 3-inch mark. At which mark is the right edge of the book for Dev?
questions.solution: The book is 9 inches long. Starting at the 3-inch mark, its right edge is 9 inches further along: 3 + 9 = 12. It is at the 12-inch mark.

solve.work: Book is 9 - 0 = 9 inches. Left edge at 3: 3 + 9 = 12.

questions.skill: Measure a length with a ruler
questions.stem: A worm's head is at the 15-inch mark of a long measuring tape and its tail is at the 6-inch mark. How many inches long is the worm?
questions.solution: Find the distance between the two marks: 15 - 6 = 9 inches.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step length problem
questions.stem: A fence has 9 sections. Each section is 8 feet long. How many feet long is the whole fence?
questions.solution: 9 sections of 8 feet each: 9 x 8 = 72 feet.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step length problem
questions.stem: A rope is 45 feet long. Jo cuts it into pieces that are each 9 feet long. How many pieces does Jo get?
questions.solution: Divide the rope into 9-foot pieces: 45 / 9 = 5. Jo gets 5 pieces.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step capacity problem
questions.stem: A tank holds 56 gallons. Pat fills it with 4 buckets that each hold the same amount of water, with none left over. How many gallons does each bucket hold?
questions.solution: Share 56 gallons equally between 4 buckets: 56 / 4 = 14. Each bucket holds 14 gallons.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step capacity problem
questions.stem: Max drinks 3 cups of water each day. How many cups of water does he drink in 7 days?
questions.solution: 7 days with 3 cups each day: 3 x 7 = 21 cups.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step weight problem
questions.stem: Sara's dog weighs 45 pounds and her cat weighs 13 pounds. How many pounds more does the dog weigh than the cat?
questions.solution: To find how much more, subtract: 45 - 13 = 32. The dog weighs 32 pounds more.

questions.skill: Solve a one-step weight problem
questions.stem: A box of 6 books that all weigh the same amount weighs 42 ounces. How many ounces does one book weigh?
questions.solution: Share the total weight between 6 books: 42 / 6 = 7. Each book weighs 7 ounces.

solve.work: 42 / 6 = 7 ounces (box weight taken as included/negligible, the usual reading).

questions.skill: Choose a reasonable estimate of a length, capacity or weight
questions.stem: Which list gives the most reasonable weights for a mouse, a dog and a car?
questions.solution: A mouse is very light, about an ounce. A dog is about 40 pounds. A car is very heavy, about 3,000 pounds. In the other lists a mouse weighs a pound, a dog is lighter than 3 pounds, or a car weighs less than a dog.

solve.work: Mouse about 1 ounce, dog about 40 pounds, car about 3,000 pounds. Other lists have a 1-lb mouse, a 40-oz dog or a 3,000-oz (about 190 lb) car.

questions.skill: Choose the best customary unit
questions.stem: Which measurement is matched with the best unit?
choices: the length of a crayon: yards
the weight of a bird feather: pounds
the capacity of a pool: gallons
the capacity of a spoon: gallons
questions.answer: the capacity of a pool: gallons
questions.solution: A pool holds a huge amount of water, so a big unit like the gallon fits. A crayon is far shorter than a yard, a feather is far lighter than a pound, and a spoon holds far less than a gallon.

solve.answer: the capacity of a pool: gallons
solve.work: A pool capacity is measured in gallons. A feather in pounds, a crayon in yards, a spoon in gallons are poor matches.

questions.skill: Read a scaled picture graph
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each apple picture stands for 5 apples. On Monday the graph shows 4 apple pictures. How many apples does Monday show?
questions.solution: Each picture is worth 5, so multiply: 4 x 5 = 20 apples.

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (one step)
questions.stem: A bar graph counts by 5s. The bar for Red ends at the 30 line. The bar for Blue ends at the 20 line. How many more students chose Red than Blue?
questions.solution: Red is 30 and Blue is 20. 30 - 20 = 10 more students chose Red.

questions.skill: Read a scaled picture graph
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each book picture stands for 10 books. The row for Tuesday has 3 book pictures. How many books does Tuesday show?
questions.solution: Each picture is worth 10 books. 3 x 10 = 30 books.

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (one step)
questions.stem: A frequency table shows the fruit students chose: Apples 8, Bananas 5, Grapes 6. How many more students chose apples than bananas?
questions.solution: Apples 8 and Bananas 5. 8 - 5 = 3 more students chose apples.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: A bar graph counts by 5s. The bar for Reading ends exactly on the line labeled 25. How many students chose Reading?
questions.solution: The line the bar ends on is labeled 25, so 25 students chose Reading. The scale counts by 5s, so the bar does not stand for 5.

questions.skill: Read a frequency table or tally chart
questions.stem: A tally chart shows that 2 groups of five tally marks and 3 more marks were made for Pizza. How many students chose Pizza?
questions.solution: Each group of five stands for 5 students. 2 x 5 = 10, and 10 + 3 = 13 students.

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (one step)
questions.stem: A bar graph counts by 2s. The bar for Birds ends at 8. The bar for Fish ends at 14. How many fewer students chose Birds than Fish?
questions.solution: Birds is 8 and Fish is 14. 14 - 8 = 6, so 6 fewer students chose Birds.

questions.skill: Read a frequency table or tally chart
questions.stem: A frequency table shows the colors students like: Red 9, Blue 12, Green 7, Yellow 10. Which color did the most students choose?
questions.solution: The biggest number in the table is 12, which is Blue.

questions.skill: Total from a graph or table
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each flower picture stands for 5 flowers. Roses have 5 pictures and Tulips have 3 pictures. How many flowers are shown in all?
questions.solution: There are 5 + 3 = 8 pictures in all. 8 x 5 = 40 flowers. (8 is only the number of pictures.)

questions.skill: Collect data into a frequency table
questions.stem: Eight students told what pet they have: dog, cat, dog, fish, dog, cat, dog, cat. How many of the students have a dog?
questions.solution: Count the dogs in the list: dog appears 4 times.

questions.skill: Read a half symbol on a scaled picture graph
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each book picture stands for 4 books. A row shows 5 whole pictures and 1 half picture. How many books does the row show?
questions.solution: A whole picture is 4 books and a half picture is half of 4, which is 2. 5 x 4 = 20, and 20 + 2 = 22 books.

questions.skill: Read a scaled bar graph
questions.stem: A bar graph counts by 10s. The bar for Basketball ends halfway between the 30 line and the 40 line. How many students chose Basketball?
questions.solution: Halfway between 30 and 40 is 35, so 35 students chose Basketball.

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (one step)
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each sticker picture stands for 5 stickers. Anna has 9 pictures and Ben has 6 pictures. How many more stickers does Anna have than Ben?
questions.solution: Anna has 9 x 5 = 45 stickers and Ben has 6 x 5 = 30 stickers. 45 - 30 = 15 more stickers.

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (one step)
questions.stem: A tally chart shows Soccer with 2 groups of five tally marks and 2 more marks, and Swimming with 1 group of five and 3 more marks. How many more students chose Soccer than Swimming?
questions.solution: Soccer is 2 x 5 + 2 = 12 and Swimming is 5 + 3 = 8. 12 - 8 = 4 more students.

questions.skill: Total from a graph or table
questions.stem: A bar graph counts by 5s. The bars end at: Apples 35, Pears 20, Plums 15, Figs 40. How many pieces of fruit are shown in all?
questions.solution: Add the four bars: 35 + 20 = 55, 55 + 15 = 70, 70 + 40 = 110 pieces of fruit.

questions.skill: Collect data into a frequency table
questions.stem: Twelve students voted for a class pet: cat, fish, dog, cat, cat, dog, fish, cat, dog, cat, fish, cat. Which frequency table matches the votes?
questions.solution: Count each pet: cat 6 times, dog 3 times, fish 3 times. 6 + 3 + 3 = 12 votes.

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (one step)
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each picture stands for 2 balls. Soccer has 7 pictures and Golf has 3 pictures. How many fewer golf balls than soccer balls are shown?
questions.solution: Soccer is 7 x 2 = 14 balls and Golf is 3 x 2 = 6 balls. 14 - 6 = 8 fewer golf balls.

questions.skill: Find or use the scale of a graph
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each picture stands for 10 stickers. Which row shows 70 stickers?
questions.solution: Each picture is 10 stickers, so 70 stickers is 70 / 10 = 7 pictures.

questions.skill: Total from a graph or table
questions.stem: A frequency table shows how students get to school: Walk 14, Bike 9, Bus 22, Car 15. How many students were counted in all?
questions.solution: Add all four: 14 + 9 = 23, 23 + 22 = 45, 45 + 15 = 60 students. (45 leaves out the Car.)

questions.skill: Choose the true statement about a graph
questions.stem: A bar graph counts by 5s. The bars end at: Pop 30, Rock 15, Jazz 20. Which statement is true?
choices: Jazz has 10 more votes than Rock
Rock has 10 fewer votes than Pop
Pop has 15 more votes than Rock
Pop has 5 more votes than Jazz
questions.answer: Pop has 15 more votes than Rock
questions.solution: Pop minus Rock is 30 - 15 = 15, so the first statement is true. Jazz minus Rock is 5, Pop minus Rock is 15 (not 10) and Pop minus Jazz is 10 (not 5).

solve.answer: Pop has 15 more votes than Rock

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (two steps)
questions.stem: A bar graph counts by 5s. The bars end at: Monday 25, Tuesday 35, Wednesday 15. How many fewer visits were there on Tuesday than on Monday and Wednesday together?
questions.solution: Monday and Wednesday together: 25 + 15 = 40. Tuesday is 35. 40 - 35 = 5 fewer visits on Tuesday.

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (two steps)
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each picture stands for 5 cups. Leo's row has 3 pictures. Mia's row has 4 more pictures than Leo's row. How many cups does Mia's row show?
questions.solution: Mia's row has 3 + 4 = 7 pictures. 7 x 5 = 35 cups.

questions.skill: Find or use the scale of a graph
questions.stem: A picture graph shows 36 students with 9 pictures, and every picture stands for the same number of students. How many students does each picture stand for?
questions.solution: Share 36 students among 9 pictures: 36 / 9 = 4 students for each picture.

questions.skill: Find or use the scale of a graph
questions.stem: A bar graph counts by 5s. The bar for Mice ends at 20. The bar for Rabbits is 3 lines taller than the bar for Mice. How many rabbits does the graph show?
questions.solution: Each line is 5 higher, so 3 lines is 3 x 5 = 15. 20 + 15 = 35 rabbits.

questions.skill: Read a half symbol on a scaled picture graph
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each picture stands for 6 pets. A row shows 3 whole pictures and 1 half picture. How many pets does the row show?
questions.solution: A whole picture is 6 pets and a half picture is 3 pets. 3 x 6 = 18, and 18 + 3 = 21 pets.

questions.skill: Collect data into a frequency table
questions.stem: A class counted the books each of 12 students read: 2, 3, 2, 4, 3, 2, 5, 3, 2, 4, 3, 2. How many more students read 2 books than read 4 books?
questions.solution: Count the 2s: there are 5. Count the 4s: there are 2. 5 - 2 = 3 more students read 2 books.

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (two steps)
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each book picture stands for 10 minutes of reading. Monday has 4 pictures. Tuesday has 2 whole pictures and 1 half picture. How many more minutes were read on Monday than on Tuesday?
questions.solution: Monday is 4 x 10 = 40 minutes. Tuesday is 2 x 10 + 5 = 25 minutes. 40 - 25 = 15 more minutes.

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (two steps)
questions.stem: A bar graph counts by 10s. The bars end at: Cats 50, Dogs 80, Birds 30, Fish 20. How many more pets are cats and dogs together than birds and fish together?
questions.solution: Cats and dogs: 50 + 80 = 130. Birds and fish: 30 + 20 = 50. 130 - 50 = 80 more pets.

questions.skill: Choose the true statement about a graph
questions.stem: A bar graph counts by 10s. The bars end at: Monday 40, Tuesday 70, Wednesday 50. Which statement is true?
choices: Monday and Wednesday together have 10 more than Tuesday
questions.solution: Tuesday minus Monday is 70 - 40 = 30, so the first statement is true. Wednesday has 20 fewer than Tuesday, Monday has 10 fewer than Wednesday, and Monday plus Wednesday is 90, which is 20 more than Tuesday.

solve.work: Tue-Mon = 30 true. Wed is 20 less than Tue; Mon+Wed = 90 is 20 more than Tue, not 10; Mon is 10 fewer than Wed, not 20.

questions.skill: How many more or fewer (two steps)
questions.stem: In a picture graph, each star stands for 5 points. Rows A and B have 6 and 8 stars. Rows C and D have 3 and 5 stars. How many fewer points do rows C and D have together than rows A and B together?
questions.solution: Rows A and B: 6 + 8 = 14 stars. Rows C and D: 3 + 5 = 8 stars. The difference is 14 - 8 = 6 stars, and 6 x 5 = 30 points.

questions.skill: Count the unit squares that cover a rectangle (rows and columns)
questions.stem: A rectangle is covered with unit squares. There are 2 rows, and each row has 3 unit squares. How many unit squares cover the rectangle?
questions.solution: Count the squares row by row: 3 + 3 = 6 unit squares.

questions.skill: Count the unit squares that cover a rectangle (rows and columns)
questions.stem: Mia covers a rectangle with unit squares. She makes 3 rows with 5 squares in each row. What is the area of the rectangle in square units?
questions.solution: Each row has 5 squares and there are 3 rows: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15. The area is 15 square units.

solve.work: 3 rows x 5 = 15 squares, area 15 square units.

questions.skill: Count the unit squares that cover a rectangle (rows and columns)
questions.stem: A rectangle is covered by 2 rows of 5 unit squares. What is its area?
questions.solution: There are 2 rows of 5 squares: 5 + 5 = 10. The area is 10 square units.

solve.work: 2 x 5 = 10 unit squares, so area 10 square units.

questions.skill: Tiling with no gaps and no overlaps
questions.stem: Sam wants to find the area of a rectangle with unit squares. How should he place the squares?
choices: Leave a small space between each pair of squares
Cover the rectangle with no gaps and no overlaps
Pile some squares on top of other squares
Cover only the border around the rectangle
questions.answer: Cover the rectangle with no gaps and no overlaps
questions.solution: To measure area, the unit squares must cover the whole rectangle, side by side, with no gaps and no overlaps.

solve.answer: Cover the rectangle with no gaps and no overlaps
solve.work: Area by tiling requires covering with no gaps and no overlaps.

questions.skill: Tiling with no gaps and no overlaps
questions.stem: What is the area of a rectangle?
choices: The number of unit squares that cover it
The number of corners where two sides meet
The distance all the way around its edge
The length of the longest side of it
questions.answer: The number of unit squares that cover it
questions.solution: Area tells how many unit squares cover a flat shape with no gaps or overlaps.

solve.answer: The number of unit squares that cover it
solve.work: Area is the number of unit squares needed to cover the shape; distance around is perimeter.

questions.skill: Compare areas by the number of unit squares
questions.stem: Rectangle X is covered by 8 unit squares. Rectangle Y is covered by 6 unit squares. Which rectangle has the greater area?
questions.solution: Both are measured with the same unit squares, and 8 is more than 6. Rectangle X has the greater area.

solve.work: 8 > 6 unit squares, so X has the greater area.

questions.skill: Find the missing number of rows or squares per row

questions.solution: Share 12 squares among 3 equal rows: 12 / 3 = 4 squares in each row.

questions.skill: Unit squares still needed on a partly covered rectangle
