questions.solution: He still needs 2 more rows of 4 squares: 4 + 4 = 8 unit squares.

solve.work: Total 3 x 4 = 12; one row of 4 down; 12 - 4 = 8 more.

questions.skill: Area is measured in square units
questions.stem: Which of these is an area?
questions.solution: Area is measured in square units. The others count lengths, corners or sides.

solve.work: Area is measured in square units: 9 square units.

questions.skill: Different rectangles with the same area
questions.stem: A rectangle has 3 rows of 4 unit squares. A second rectangle has the same area and has 2 rows. How many unit squares are in each row of the second rectangle?
questions.solution: The first rectangle has 3 x 4 = 12 unit squares. The second has 12 squares in 2 equal rows: 12 / 2 = 6 in each row.

solve.work: First area 3 x 4 = 12; 2 rows: 12 / 2 = 6 per row.

questions.skill: Count the unit squares that cover a rectangle (rows and columns)
questions.stem: A rectangle is covered with unit squares in 6 rows of 4 squares each. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: Six rows of 4 squares: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 24. The area is 24 square units.

questions.skill: Count the unit squares that cover a rectangle (rows and columns)
questions.stem: Kai tiles the floor of a toy house with unit squares. He makes 5 rows with 7 squares in each row. How many unit squares does he use?
questions.solution: Five rows of 7 squares: 5 x 7 = 35 unit squares.

questions.skill: Tiling with no gaps and no overlaps
questions.stem: Dev covers a rectangle with unit squares but leaves small gaps between them. Why is his count not the area of the rectangle?
choices: A rectangle that is covered in squares has no area
Only the squares in the four corners can be counted
The squares must all be different sizes from each other
Some of the rectangle is not covered by squares
questions.answer: Some of the rectangle is not covered by squares
questions.solution: Area counts unit squares that cover the whole rectangle. With gaps, part of the rectangle is left uncovered, so the count is too small.

solve.answer: Some of the rectangle is not covered by squares
solve.work: Gaps leave parts of the rectangle uncovered, so the count is short of the area.

questions.skill: Tiling with no gaps and no overlaps
questions.stem: Lena covers a rectangle with unit squares and some squares overlap. She counts every square. What is true about her count?
choices: It is exactly right, because every square is counted
It is too big, because some space is covered twice
It is too small, because some squares are missing
It is the distance around the whole rectangle
questions.answer: It is too big, because some space is covered twice
questions.solution: Overlapping squares cover the same space more than once, so counting every square gives more than the area.

solve.answer: It is too big, because some space is covered twice
solve.work: Overlapping squares cover some space twice, so counting every square overcounts.

questions.skill: Compare areas by the number of unit squares
questions.stem: Rectangle P is covered by 4 rows of 6 unit squares. Rectangle Q is covered by 3 rows of 7 unit squares. How many more unit squares cover P than Q?
questions.solution: P has 4 x 6 = 24 squares and Q has 3 x 7 = 21 squares. 24 - 21 = 3 more.

questions.skill: Compare areas by the number of unit squares
questions.stem: Mat A has 5 rows of 6 unit squares. Mat B has 4 rows of 8 unit squares. Which mat has the greater area?
questions.solution: Mat A has 5 x 6 = 30 squares. Mat B has 4 x 8 = 32 squares. Mat B has the greater area.

solve.work: A = 5 x 6 = 30, B = 4 x 8 = 32; B is greater.

questions.skill: Find the missing number of rows or squares per row
questions.stem: A rectangle is covered by 28 unit squares. Each row has 7 squares. How many rows are there?
questions.solution: Each row has 7 squares, so the number of rows is 28 / 7 = 4.

questions.skill: Unit squares still needed on a partly covered rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangle needs 6 rows of 8 unit squares to cover it. Sam has put down 4 rows. How many more unit squares does he need?
questions.solution: He needs 2 more rows of 8 squares: 2 x 8 = 16 unit squares.

questions.skill: Area is measured in square units
questions.stem: Which statement about a unit square is true?
choices: It has an area of 4 square units
It has a length of 1 square unit
It has an area of 1 square unit
questions.answer: It has an area of 1 square unit
questions.solution: A unit square is the unit for measuring area, so covering it needs exactly one unit square: its area is 1 square unit.

solve.answer: It has an area of 1 square unit
solve.work: A unit square has side 1 unit and area 1 square unit.

questions.skill: Different rectangles with the same area
questions.stem: A rectangle with 3 rows of 8 unit squares has the same area as a second rectangle with 4 rows. How many unit squares are in each row of the second rectangle?
questions.solution: The first rectangle has 3 x 8 = 24 unit squares. The second has 24 squares in 4 equal rows: 24 / 4 = 6 in each row.

questions.skill: Count the unit squares that cover a rectangle (rows and columns)
questions.stem: A rectangle is covered by unit squares in 9 rows with 8 squares in each row. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: Nine rows of 8 squares: 9 x 8 = 72. The area is 72 square units.

questions.skill: Compare areas by the number of unit squares
questions.stem: Rectangle R is covered by 9 rows of 6 unit squares. Rectangle S is covered by 7 rows of 8 unit squares. How many more unit squares cover S than R?
questions.solution: R has 9 x 6 = 54 squares and S has 7 x 8 = 56 squares. 56 - 54 = 2 more.

questions.skill: Compare areas by the number of unit squares
questions.stem: Four rectangles are covered by unit squares. Which rectangle has the greatest area?
questions.solution: The areas are 7 x 6 = 42, 5 x 9 = 45, 8 x 5 = 40 and 4 x 10 = 40. The greatest is 45 square units.

questions.skill: Find the missing number of rows or squares per row
questions.stem: A rectangle is covered by 56 unit squares in rows of 8. How many rows are there?
questions.solution: Each row has 8 squares, so there are 56 / 8 = 7 rows.

questions.skill: Find the missing number of rows or squares per row
questions.stem: A rectangle is covered by 63 unit squares in 7 equal rows. How many unit squares are in each row?
questions.solution: Share 63 squares among 7 equal rows: 63 / 7 = 9 squares in each row.

questions.skill: Unit squares still needed on a partly covered rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangle needs 7 rows of 9 unit squares to cover it. Gia has covered 5 rows. How many more unit squares does she need?
questions.solution: She needs 2 more rows of 9 squares: 2 x 9 = 18 unit squares.

questions.skill: Unit squares still needed on a partly covered rectangle
questions.stem: A rectangle needs 6 rows of 9 unit squares to cover it. Tom has put down 37 unit squares so far. How many more unit squares does he need?
questions.solution: The rectangle needs 6 x 9 = 54 unit squares. He has 37, so he needs 54 - 37 = 17 more.

questions.skill: Area is measured in square units
questions.stem: The area of a rectangle is 24 square units. What does the 24 tell you?
choices: Each of its sides is exactly 24 units long
It takes 24 unit squares to cover it exactly
It has 24 rows of unit squares in it
It has 24 corners where its sides meet
questions.answer: It takes 24 unit squares to cover it exactly
questions.solution: An area of 24 square units means 24 unit squares exactly cover the rectangle.

solve.answer: It takes 24 unit squares to cover it exactly
solve.work: Area 24 square units means 24 unit squares cover it with no gaps or overlaps.

questions.skill: Different rectangles with the same area
questions.stem: Which rectangle has the same area as a rectangle with 6 rows of 4 unit squares?
questions.solution: The first rectangle has 6 x 4 = 24 squares. Only 3 x 8 = 24. The others have 25, 28 and 36 squares.

questions.skill: Area from rows of unit squares
questions.stem: Maya covers a rectangle with unit squares, with no gaps and no overlaps. There are 3 rows with 5 squares in each row. What is the area of the rectangle in square units?
questions.solution: There are 3 rows of 5 squares, so the area is $3 \times 5 = 15$ square units.

questions.skill: Area from the side lengths
questions.stem: A rectangular mat is 6 feet long and 4 feet wide. What is its area?
questions.solution: Area is length times width: $6 \times 4 = 24$ square feet. Adding the sides gives 10 and the distance around the mat is 20, neither of which is the area.

questions.skill: Area from rows of unit squares
questions.stem: A rectangle is covered with unit squares in 5 rows of 8 squares. Which number sentence gives its area in square units?
questions.solution: Area is the number of rows times the number of squares in each row: $5 \times 8 = 40$.

questions.skill: Area as repeated addition of rows
questions.stem: A rectangle has 4 rows of 3 unit squares. Which addition sentence gives its area in square units?
questions.solution: Each of the 4 rows has 3 squares, so add 3 four times: $3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12$ square units.

questions.skill: Area from the side lengths
questions.stem: Which rectangle has an area of 18 square units?
questions.solution: $3 \times 6 = 18$. The others have areas $4 \times 5 = 20$, $2 \times 8 = 16$ and $3 \times 9 = 27$.

questions.skill: Splitting a rectangle into two rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangle that is 5 units tall and 6 units wide is split into a 5 by 4 rectangle with area 20 and a 5 by 2 rectangle with area 10. What is the area of the whole 5 by 6 rectangle in square units?
questions.solution: The area of the whole rectangle is the sum of the areas of its two parts: $20 + 10 = 30$ square units. It also equals $5 \times 6 = 30$.

questions.skill: Area as repeated addition of rows
questions.stem: Lena finds the area of a rectangle by adding the squares in each row: $8 + 8 + 8$. How many rows of squares does the rectangle have?
questions.solution: She added 8 three times, once for each row. So the rectangle has 3 rows, and its area is $8 \times 3 = 24$ square units.

solve.work: 8 is added three times, so 3 rows of 8.

questions.skill: Splitting a rectangle into two rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangle 3 units tall and 8 units wide is split into a 3 by 5 rectangle and a 3 by 3 rectangle. Which number sentence is true?
questions.solution: The area of the whole rectangle equals the sum of the areas of the two parts: $3 \times 8 = 15 + 9 = 24$.

questions.skill: Adding the areas of non-overlapping rectangles
questions.stem: An L-shaped floor is made of two rectangles that do not overlap. One rectangle is 5 feet by 2 feet. The other is 3 feet by 2 feet. What is the area of the L-shaped floor in square feet?
questions.solution: The first rectangle has area $5 \times 2 = 10$ and the second has area $3 \times 2 = 6$. Together: $10 + 6 = 16$ square feet.

questions.skill: Area from the side lengths
questions.stem: A rectangular garden is 9 meters long and 2 meters wide. What is its area in square meters?
questions.solution: Area is length times width: $9 \times 2 = 18$ square meters.

questions.skill: Splitting a rectangle into two rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangle that is 4 units tall and 9 units wide is split by one straight line into a 4 by 5 rectangle and a 4 by 4 rectangle. What is the area of the whole rectangle in square units?
questions.solution: The parts have areas $4 \times 5 = 20$ and $4 \times 4 = 16$. Add them: $20 + 16 = 36$ square units.

questions.skill: Splitting a rectangle into two rectangles
questions.stem: Aisha wants the area of a rectangle that is 7 units by 6 units. She splits the 6 units into two parts and multiplies each part by 7. Which way of splitting does NOT give the area of the whole rectangle?
questions.solution: The two parts of the 6 must add to 6. Here $5 + 2 = 7$, so $7 \times 5 + 7 \times 2 = 49$ is too big. The others use parts that add to 6 and give $7 \times 6 = 42$.

solve.work: 3+3=6, 4+2=6, 1+5=6 all split 6; 5+2=7 does not, giving 49 not 42.

questions.skill: Adding the areas of non-overlapping rectangles
questions.stem: A patio is L-shaped. It is made of one rectangle that is 8 meters by 3 meters and another that is 4 meters by 2 meters. They do not overlap. What is the area of the patio in square meters?
questions.solution: $8 \times 3 = 24$ and $4 \times 2 = 8$. Together: $24 + 8 = 32$ square meters.

questions.skill: Area from the side lengths
questions.stem: A rectangular playground is 9 meters long and 8 meters wide. What is its area in square meters?
questions.solution: Multiply the length by the width: $9 \times 8 = 72$ square meters.

questions.skill: Area from rows of unit squares
questions.stem: Rectangle P is covered by 4 rows of 6 unit squares. Which rectangle has the same area as rectangle P?
questions.solution: Rectangle P has $4 \times 6 = 24$ unit squares. Three rows of 8 is $3 \times 8 = 24$. The others have 25, 28 and 20.

questions.skill: Area as repeated addition of rows
questions.stem: The area of a rectangle can be found by adding $9 + 9 + 9 + 9$. Which multiplication sentence gives the same area?
questions.solution: Adding 9 four times is $4 \times 9 = 36$.

questions.skill: Adding the areas of non-overlapping rectangles
questions.stem: A shape is made of a 6 by 3 rectangle and a 2 by 3 rectangle that touch along a side and do not overlap. Which expression gives the area of the shape?
questions.solution: Find the area of each rectangle and add: $6 \times 3 + 2 \times 3 = 18 + 6 = 24$ square units.

questions.skill: Area from the side lengths
questions.stem: Which rectangle has the greatest area?
questions.solution: The areas are $4 \times 8 = 32$, $6 \times 5 = 30$, $3 \times 9 = 27$ and $7 \times 4 = 28$. The greatest is 32.

questions.skill: Area from rows of unit squares
questions.stem: A floor is covered with square tiles that are each 1 foot on a side, in 8 rows with 7 tiles in each row. What is the area of the floor in square feet?
questions.solution: The floor has $8 \times 7 = 56$ tiles that are each 1 square foot, so its area is 56 square feet.

questions.skill: Split a rectangle into two smaller rectangles
questions.stem: Ana covers a board with sticky notes, with no gaps and no overlaps. Each note is 1 square unit. The top part has 4 rows with 9 notes in each row. The bottom part has 3 rows with 9 notes in each row. What is the area of the board in square units?
questions.solution: The top part has $4 \times 9 = 36$ notes. The bottom part has $3 \times 9 = 27$ notes. The area is $36 + 27 = 63$ square units. This is the same as 7 rows of 9.

questions.skill: Adding the areas of non-overlapping rectangles
questions.stem: A room is L-shaped. It is made of a 9 by 6 rectangle and a 5 by 4 rectangle that do not overlap. All lengths are in feet. What is the area of the room in square feet?
questions.solution: $9 \times 6 = 54$ and $5 \times 4 = 20$. Together: $54 + 20 = 74$ square feet.

questions.skill: Splitting a rectangle into two rectangles
questions.stem: A rectangle is 9 units tall and 11 units wide. It is split into a 9 by 10 rectangle and a 9 by 1 rectangle. What is the area of the whole rectangle in square units?
questions.solution: $9 \times 10 = 90$ and $9 \times 1 = 9$. Add the two areas: $90 + 9 = 99$ square units.

questions.skill: Splitting a rectangle into two rectangles
questions.stem: A 6 by 8 rectangle is split into a 6 by 3 rectangle and a 6 by 5 rectangle. Which statement is true?
choices: The two smaller areas added together are more than the area of the 6 by 8 rectangle
The two smaller areas added together equal the area of the 6 by 8 rectangle
The area of the 6 by 8 rectangle is the sum of its length and width
Each smaller area is the same as the area of the 6 by 8 rectangle
questions.answer: The two smaller areas added together equal the area of the 6 by 8 rectangle
questions.solution: Splitting a rectangle does not change its total area, so the parts add up to the whole: $18 + 30 = 48 = 6 \times 8$.

solve.answer: The two smaller areas added together equal the area of the 6 by 8 rectangle

questions.skill: Adding the areas of non-overlapping rectangles
questions.stem: A shape is made from a 10 by 3 rectangle and a 4 by 5 rectangle that do not overlap. Which number sentence gives the area of the shape?
questions.solution: $10 \times 3 = 30$ and $4 \times 5 = 20$, and $30 + 20 = 50$ square units.

questions.skill: Unknown side from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 32 square units and one side that is 4 units long. The other side is ? units long, where $4 \times ? = 32$. What is the ?
questions.solution: We need a number that makes $4 \times ? = 32$. Since $4 \times 8 = 32$, the other side is 8 units.

questions.skill: Unknown side from the area
questions.stem: A rectangle has an area of 40 square units. Its length is 3 units more than its width. What is the width in units?
questions.solution: Look for two numbers that multiply to 40 and differ by 3. $8 \times 5 = 40$ and $8 - 5 = 3$. So the width is 5 units.

solve.work: Factor pairs of 40: 1x40, 2x20, 4x10, 5x8. Differ by 3: 5 and 8. Width 5.

questions.skill: Adding the areas of non-overlapping rectangles
questions.stem: A figure is made of three rectangles that do not overlap. They measure 3 by 4, 2 by 5, and 6 by 2. What is the area of the figure in square units?
questions.solution: $3 \times 4 = 12$, $2 \times 5 = 10$ and $6 \times 2 = 12$. Together: $12 + 10 + 12 = 34$ square units.

questions.skill: Area from the side lengths
questions.stem: Rectangle A is 6 units by 7 units. Rectangle B is 5 units by 9 units. What is the area, in square units, of the rectangle with the greater area?
questions.solution: Rectangle A has area $6 \times 7 = 42$ and rectangle B has area $5 \times 9 = 45$. The greater area is 45.

questions.skill: Splitting a rectangle into two rectangles
questions.stem: A 6 by 8 rectangle is cut straight down the middle into two rectangles of the same size, each 6 by 4. Which number sentence gives the area of the whole rectangle?
questions.solution: Each half has area $6 \times 4 = 24$. Two halves make $24 + 24 = 48$, which is also $6 \times 8$.

questions.skill: Adding the areas of non-overlapping rectangles
questions.stem: A pool cover is a rectangle 9 feet long and 7 feet wide. A second cover is a square, 6 feet on each side. What is the total area of the two covers?
questions.solution: The first cover has area $9 \times 7 = 63$ and the second has area $6 \times 6 = 36$. Together: $63 + 36 = 99$ square feet.

questions.skill: perimeter of a triangle
questions.stem: A triangle has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Perimeter is the distance around a shape. Add the three sides: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 cm.

questions.skill: perimeter of a polygon with more sides
questions.stem: A shape with 4 sides has sides of 7 in, 5 in, 6 in and 8 in. What is its perimeter, in inches?
questions.solution: Add the four sides: 7 + 5 = 12, 12 + 6 = 18, 18 + 8 = 26 in.

questions.skill: unknown side of a triangle or polygon from the perimeter
questions.stem: A triangle has a perimeter of 15 cm. Two of its sides are 6 cm and 4 cm long. How long is the third side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The three sides add up to 15. The two known sides make 6 + 4 = 10. The third side is 15 - 10 = 5 cm.

questions.skill: side of a regular polygon or square from the perimeter
questions.stem: A square has a perimeter of 60 cm. How long is each side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A square has 4 equal sides. 60 divided by 4 is 15, since 4 x 15 = 60. Each side is 15 cm. (240 comes from multiplying by 4, and 30 from dividing by 2.)

questions.skill: perimeter of a rectangle or square
questions.stem: A rectangle is 8 feet long and 3 feet wide. What is its perimeter, in feet?
questions.solution: A rectangle has two lengths and two widths. 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 feet.

questions.skill: perimeter of a regular polygon
questions.stem: A regular pentagon has 5 sides that are all 4 cm long. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: All 5 sides are equal, so the perimeter is 5 groups of 4. 5 x 4 = 20 cm.

questions.skill: perimeter of a rectangle or square
questions.stem: A square has sides that are each 6 inches long. What is its perimeter?
questions.solution: A square has 4 equal sides. 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24 inches.

questions.skill: perimeter in a story
questions.stem: Jin walks once around the edge of a rectangular garden. The garden is 9 meters long and 4 meters wide. How many meters does Jin walk?
questions.solution: Walking once around the edge is the perimeter. 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 meters.

questions.skill: what perimeter means
questions.stem: What does the perimeter of a flat shape tell you?
choices: How far it is around the outside
How much space is inside it
How long its longest side is
questions.answer: How far it is around the outside
questions.solution: Perimeter is the distance around the outside of a shape. The space inside is its area.

solve.answer: How far it is around the outside
solve.work: Perimeter is the distance around the outside.

questions.skill: perimeter of a polygon with more sides
questions.stem: A hexagon has 6 sides. Its sides are 2 m, 3 m, 2 m, 3 m, 2 m and 3 m long. What is its perimeter?
questions.solution: Add all 6 sides: 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 = 15 m. The wrong answers leave a side out or use one length for every side.

questions.skill: perimeter in a story
questions.stem: A rectangular poster is 24 inches long and 18 inches wide. Ravi glues ribbon along all four edges. How many inches of ribbon does he need?
questions.solution: The ribbon goes around the poster, so find the perimeter: 24 + 18 + 24 + 18 = 84 inches.

questions.skill: comparing perimeters
questions.stem: Rectangle A is 12 cm long and 2 cm wide. Rectangle B is 7 cm long and 5 cm wide. Which rectangle has the greater perimeter, and by how much?
questions.solution: Rectangle A: 12 + 2 + 12 + 2 = 28 cm. Rectangle B: 7 + 5 + 7 + 5 = 24 cm. A is greater by 28 - 24 = 4 cm. (Rectangle B has more space inside, but that is area, not perimeter.)

questions.skill: perimeter of a polygon with more sides
questions.stem: A shape has 6 straight sides that measure 10 cm, 6 cm, 4 cm, 3 cm, 6 cm and 3 cm. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Add all six sides: 10 + 6 + 4 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 32 cm.

questions.skill: perimeter in a story
questions.stem: A square park has sides that are each 120 meters long. Dev jogs once around the edge of the park. How far does he jog, in meters?
questions.solution: The edge of the park is its perimeter. A square has 4 equal sides, so 4 x 120 = 480 meters.

questions.skill: unknown side of a rectangle from the perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is 9 cm. What is its width, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The length and width together make half the perimeter: 30 divided by 2 = 15 cm. The width is 15 - 9 = 6 cm.

questions.skill: unknown side of a triangle or polygon from the perimeter
questions.stem: A shape with 5 sides has a perimeter of 37 cm. Four of its sides are 8 cm, 6 cm, 9 cm and 6 cm long. How long is the fifth side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The four known sides add to 8 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 29 cm. The fifth side is 37 - 29 = 8 cm.

questions.skill: perimeter of a polygon with more sides
questions.stem: A pentagon has sides of 12 cm, 9 cm, 7 cm, 10 cm and 8 cm. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Add all five sides: 12 + 9 + 7 + 10 + 8 = 46 cm. Leaving out the 10 cm gives 36, leaving out the 8 cm gives 38.

questions.skill: side of a regular polygon or square from the perimeter
questions.stem: A regular hexagon has a perimeter of 42 cm. How long is one side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides. 42 divided by 6 is 7, so each side is 7 cm.

questions.skill: perimeter of a triangle
questions.stem: A triangle has two sides that are each 14 cm long and a third side that is 9 cm long. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Add all three sides, counting the 14 cm side twice: 14 + 14 + 9 = 37 cm.

questions.skill: unknown side of a triangle or polygon from the perimeter
questions.stem: A triangle has a perimeter of 29 cm. Two of its sides are 11 cm and 8 cm long. How long is the third side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The known sides add to 11 + 8 = 19 cm. The third side is 29 - 19 = 10 cm.

questions.skill: unknown side of a rectangle from the perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 40 cm. Which could be its length and width?
questions.solution: Length plus width must be half the perimeter, 20 cm. Only 14 + 6 = 20 works. 25 + 15 = 40 would give a perimeter of 80 cm.

questions.skill: perimeter in a story
questions.stem: A farmer builds a fence around a rectangular pen that is 18 meters long and 12 meters wide. Each meter of fence costs 4 dollars. How many dollars does the fence cost?
questions.solution: The fence goes around the pen, so find the perimeter: 18 + 12 + 18 + 12 = 60 meters. Then 60 x 4 = 240 dollars.

questions.skill: unknown side of a triangle or polygon from the perimeter
questions.stem: A triangle has sides of 25 cm and 17 cm and a third side of unknown length. Its perimeter is 70 cm. How long is the third side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The two known sides add to 25 + 17 = 42 cm. The third side is 70 - 42 = 28 cm.

questions.skill: unknown side of a triangle or polygon from the perimeter
questions.stem: A triangle has a perimeter of 45 cm. One side is 13 cm long, and the other two sides are equal in length. How long is each of the equal sides, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The two equal sides together are 45 - 13 = 32 cm. Each one is 32 divided by 2 = 16 cm.

questions.skill: unknown side of a triangle or polygon from the perimeter
questions.stem: A pentagon has a perimeter of 53 cm. Three of its sides are 9 cm each, one side is 11 cm, and the last side is unknown. How long is the last side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The three sides of 9 cm make 27 cm. With the 11 cm side that is 27 + 11 = 38 cm. The last side is 53 - 38 = 15 cm.

questions.skill: perimeter of a shape made from other shapes
questions.stem: Three squares, each with sides of 5 cm, are placed in a row with their sides touching to make one long rectangle. What is the perimeter of the rectangle, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The rectangle is 3 x 5 = 15 cm long and 5 cm wide. Its perimeter is 15 + 5 + 15 + 5 = 40 cm.

questions.skill: perimeter of a polygon with more sides
questions.stem: A hexagon has two sides of 15 cm and four sides of 8 cm. What is its perimeter, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Two sides of 15 make 30 cm. Four sides of 8 make 32 cm. 30 + 32 = 62 cm.

questions.skill: comparing perimeters
questions.stem: Which shape has the greatest perimeter?
choices: A rectangle that is 12 cm long and 5 cm wide
A triangle with sides of 10 cm, 11 cm and 12 cm
A regular pentagon with sides of 7 cm
A square with sides of 9 cm
questions.answer: A square with sides of 9 cm
questions.solution: Square: 4 x 9 = 36 cm. Rectangle: 12 + 5 + 12 + 5 = 34 cm. Triangle: 10 + 11 + 12 = 33 cm. Pentagon: 5 x 7 = 35 cm. The square is greatest.

solve.answer: A square with sides of 9 cm
solve.work: Rectangle 2(12+5) = 34; triangle 33; square 36; pentagon 35. The square is greatest.

questions.skill: unknown side of a rectangle from the perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 46 cm and a width of 7 cm. What is its length, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Half the perimeter is 46 divided by 2 = 23 cm, which is one length plus one width. The length is 23 - 7 = 16 cm.

questions.skill: unknown side of a rectangle from the perimeter
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 56 cm and a length of 16 cm. What is its width, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Half the perimeter is 56 divided by 2 = 28 cm, which is length plus width. The width is 28 - 16 = 12 cm. (Check: 16 + 12 + 16 + 12 = 56.) The answer 28 is only half the perimeter; 40 subtracts the length once from the whole perimeter.

questions.skill: Count the sides and square corners of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: A quadrilateral is a closed flat shape with straight sides. How many sides does every quadrilateral have?
questions.solution: The word quadrilateral means a shape with 4 sides. Every quadrilateral has 4 sides.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its sides and corners
questions.stem: A flat shape has 4 straight sides that are all the same length and 4 square corners. What is it?
questions.solution: A square has 4 sides that are all the same length and 4 square corners. A triangle has 3 sides, a pentagon 5 and a hexagon 6.

solve.work: 4 equal sides and 4 square corners: a square.

questions.skill: Count the sides and square corners of quadrilaterals
questions.stem: How many square corners does a square have?
questions.solution: All 4 corners of a square are square corners.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its sides and corners
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 sides that are all the same length. Its corners are not square corners. What is it?
questions.solution: A shape with 4 equal sides is a rhombus. A square would have 4 square corners, and a rectangle would too, so it is a rhombus.

solve.work: 4 equal sides without square corners: a rhombus (not a square).
